Such a page was therefore listed at open and never updated again while the app stayed open. Conflict copies stay routed (they are not eligible text but must refresh the conflicts panel); excluded trees (assets/, dot-directories, logseq/bak/) stay excluded on both the routing and the force-a-full-scan paths, so dropping an image into assets/ still cannot trigger a graph rescan. entries.title: A network-share (poll-mode) graph keeps its save-time admission index warm instead of rebuilding the whole graph on every save
entries.notes: When the watcher runs in poll mode (a network share, or TINE_WATCH=poll), every 3 s cycle invalidated the guarded graph-text admission index unconditionally before reconciling. Since a Direct save consults that index and rebuilds it when invalid -- a two-pass byte-retaining walk of the whole graph -- such a user could never hold a warm index and paid a full-graph rebuild on essentially every save. The blanket invalidation was compensating for the poll rescan being narrower than the index (journals/+pages/ vs graph-wide); once REG-EXTERNAL-GRAPH-WIDE-EVENTS-268 widened the rescan to the same scope, the rescan's own result became a complete account of what changed and is published as exact observations instead. Ordering is load-bearing and asserted: the observation happens after the scan and BEFORE any reconcile, so the index is never staler than the scan that produced it -- the same window the inotify callback lane already had, not a wider one. A scan that could not read part of the graph reports itself incomplete and still invalidates. Fail-before proven by restoring the blanket invalidation in place: the quiet-cycle test then reported invalidated: true with complete_builds unchanged at 1.

entries.title: Saving an existing page never captures or reparses the whole graph
entries.notes: Reopened after the reporter confirmed the defect remained in v0.6.91 Direct Files. The diagnostic refusal was `precheck.limit: guarded graph-text identity construction failed: initial shadow peak build memory bound exceeded`; GH #295 independently measured one complete 1,046-file / 16.7 MB capture on every Windows save (roughly 0.9-1.1 s). Root cause was architectural: both existing-target validation and the atomic replacement transaction invoked the complete managed shadow-import admission index. The cut keeps an existing save local: one exact target parse/read, one capability-safe traversal following only portable-equivalent target path components (including case/NFC aliases in ancestor directories), exact file identity and link-count-one checks, and the existing no-replace/retire/restore/fsync protocol. Missing-target creation now uses its separate single-census cached-evidence proof recorded by REG-DIRECT-CREATE-RETAINED-SHADOW-LIMIT-249-266. On the attached #295 graph in release mode, warm save median was 1.13 ms and forcibly invalidated save median 0.98 ms, with complete builds unchanged at one; the prior current-master measurement was 2.75 ms warm and 70 ms invalidated. Structural tests prove exactly one portable traversal, zero graph capture enumerations, one target parse, and no write on portable/hard-link/external-byte conflicts.

entries.title: Creating a Direct Files page does not build the managed shadow-import retained-byte inventory or strand the edit behind precheck.limit
entries.notes: Post-v0.6.92 reporter evidence revoked the complete save/reopen claim for GH #249 without disproving its Windows-safe filename codec: the timestamp page reaches the editor but save fails with the exact diagnostic `precheck.limit: guarded graph-text identity construction failed: initial shadow peak build memory bound exceeded`. GH #266's v0.6.92 Windows trace records the same 12.8-14.2 s refusal three times while instrumented graph open itself takes 18 ms, leaving open/switch blocked for about 41 s and close eventually offering to discard unsaved work. Commit 0394d6e0 correctly cut the complete admission index from existing-target saves, but deliberately left missing-target creation and its atomic writer on the two-pass byte-retaining managed shadow-import capture. The source fix binds the generation-current parsed identity index, exact cached disk revisions, and page-index failures to one capability/no-follow streaming census; creation retains paths, digests, resource identities, and link counts only, applies the retained raw-byte ceiling per file rather than cumulatively, performs no save-time graph parse or retained-byte capture, fails closed without retry, and gives the resulting proof to the exact no-replace publisher. A final streaming census immediately before no-replace publication closes GH #321's external cross-path race without parsing or retaining graph bytes; deterministic hook tests cover both a portable alias and a distinct path claiming the same semantic title. Identity-preserving existing saves advance warm semantic evidence in O(1), while explicit-title identity changes replace it coherently. Creation refuses portable case/NFC target aliases including ancestors, historical graph extensions and arbitrary eligible paths, explicit semantic owners, hard links/resource aliases, symlink parents/leaves, stale same-length retitles, generation changes, and exact-target or cross-path races without changing incumbent or outside bytes. Existing exact-target saves preserve the prior traversal rule: noncolliding siblings under portable-equivalent or symlink ancestor neighbors do not block the save, while a colliding leaf still refuses. A test-only initial-capture charge equal to the parent peak limit proved the parent failed locally with the exact suffix `initial shadow peak build memory bound exceeded`, classifier `precheck.limit`, and no created file; the same armed limit is untouched by the fixed creation path. This construction used generated temporary graph data only. The reversible timestamp codec is exercised in both filename formats. Packaged Windows pass-after remains required before a released Windows claim.

entries.title: A page whose file was replaced with identical content can still be saved instead of stranding the edit
entries.notes: A save proves it is not clobbering someone else's work two ways: base_rev must still match the bytes on disk, AND the file must still be the same physical file read at load. External tools break the second without touching the first -- OneDrive rehydrating a Files-On-Demand placeholder, a Syncthing pull landing identical bytes, cp over a hardlink. Every later save then failed with 'existing page identity changed since load', and BOTH exits from the resulting conflict prompt were dead ends: Keep-mine re-ran the same check and failed too, and Use-disk-version discarded the user's edit. The watcher now re-pins the retained identity when, and only when, the retained revision still matches the bytes now on disk, so the proof it stands on is unchanged. Fail-before proven by disabling the re-pin in place. The control (a replace that also changes the bytes) still conflicts and still writes nothing, and is asserted alongside.

entries.title: A symlink inside the graph does not make every other page unsaveable
entries.notes: One symlink in a descended, non-excluded scope (graph root, pages/, journals/, a custom folder) aborted the save-time admission capture, and because every Direct save takes that capture to answer a filename question, the whole graph became read-only -- the user's OTHER pages could not be saved either. Skipping is what the rest of Tine already does: every traversal is no-follow, the watcher snapshot never descends a symlinked directory, and graph_inventory_entry never admits a symlinked file, so the capture was the only place escalating a non-entity to a fatal error. The shadow-import bootstrap capture still refuses, asserted separately: an import that silently leaves out a file the user considers part of their graph is a worse failure than a refused import. NOTE the audit's own repro for this finding is WRONG -- it used assets/, which is fixed-excluded, so that experiment goes green and would retire a real finding; both halves are asserted in one test so nobody re-runs it. Known bounded gap: a symlink is no longer a member of the portable-key collision group, matching discovery, which never knew about it either.

entries.title: Save failures that a conflict prompt cannot resolve are reported as themselves, not as a content conflict
entries.notes: The backend collapsed EVERY io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists to the literal string 'conflict', and the frontend recognised a conflict by testing whether the message CONTAINED that substring. A portable-filename collision, a physical-resource alias, a symlink refusal and 'another document owns this page identity' therefore all raised the content-conflict prompt, whose only options are Keep-mine and Use-disk-version -- neither of which can resolve any of them. Choosing either left the page marked conflicted, and a conflicted page silently refuses to save from then on, so the user's page was stranded by an error message. Only a real base-revision conflict carries the 'conflict' contract now; everything else carries its bounded D0 failure code as a stable prefix and falls through to the retryable path. The frontend match is exact rather than substring. Fail-before is structural and asserted directly on the mapping function.

entries.title: A generation change during the Direct creation census fails closed without repeated whole-graph work
entries.notes: The former Direct missing-target admission capture ran two byte-retaining full-graph passes and retried their disagreement, amplifying unrelated concurrent filesystem activity into repeated whole-graph work. Ordinary Direct creation no longer enters that managed shadow-import capture. It performs one capability/no-follow streaming evidence census, binds it to the generation-current cached semantic snapshot, then performs one final streaming census immediately before publication to detect external cross-path races. Neither census parses or retains graph bytes, and disagreement fails closed without retry or mutation. The deterministic generation-change and final-publication hooks prove bounded work and unchanged neighboring bytes.

entries.title: A save failure a retry cannot change is reported once instead of re-running the whole check three times

tests: src/persistence.test.ts::does not retry failures a retry cannot change

entries.notes: scheduleTransientRetry re-ran a failed save at 100 ms and 300 ms before toasting -- three full attempts per dirty page. Each attempt re-runs the whole pre-save admission check, which on a large graph is the expensive part, only to reach the same answer for a failure class that cannot change on retry: a portable-filename collision, a physical-resource alias, a symlink in scope, a non-portable path, a nofollow refusal, a limit breach, or another page already owning the title. #267's 'about a minute, then a red toast' is that multiplier on top of an already slow check. Those classes now report once; genuinely transient ones (precheck.interrupted, identity.changed_since_load, unclassified I/O) still retry. Depends on REG-SAVE-ERROR-MISCLASSIFIED-AS-CONFLICT-001 for the bounded codes that make the distinction possible.

entries.title: Resolving a save conflict with "keep mine" overwrites the file, including after a real external change
entries.notes: force_save_page proved its right to write the pinned file from PageDto.rev, which pageToDto never sets -- ordinary saves carry the load revision in the separate base_rev argument, as the parameter's own comment said. With rev=None the retained-owner check could not hold, so every override failed AlreadyExists 'path-pinned page does not match its captured exact owner', leaving discard-my-edits as the only working exit from the conflict prompt. The suite missed it because every test force-saved a load_named/load_by_path DTO, which does carry rev=Some -- a shape the wire never produces. Replaced the untyped revision argument with an explicit PinnedSaveAuthority. Audit 2026-08-06 N1 (Critical).

entries.title: An unclassified save failure reports what happened instead of raising an unresolvable conflict prompt
entries.notes: direct_save_failure_code ended with a catch-all mapping any AlreadyExists to conflict.other, which commands.rs turned into the literal 'conflict' -- the string that raises the keep-mine/use-disk banner. About forty-five other conditions raise AlreadyExists (managed and projection internals, reservation and page-name collisions) for which neither button helps and 'use disk' discards the user's edits; the mapping also replaced the message text, so a failure that had RETAINED those edits under a recovery name arrived as a bare unexplained conflict. conflict.* membership is now decided by naming a condition. Audit 2026-08-06 N3 (High) and the still-open half of N2.

entries.title: A conflict resolution during a cross-page move waits for the destination write instead of writing the moved block out of existence

tests: src/persistenceMoveBarrier.test.ts::defers a keep-mine on a held source, then applies it on release

entries.notes: heldSources holds a moved subtree's SOURCE pages until the DESTINATION write is durable, so the block is never in neither place. The guard read heldSources.has(name) && !force, so a forced save walked through it. Latent while force-save could not reach the backend (N1); live once it could. A deferred keep-mine is now remembered and re-issued when the destination lands, because the ordinary save path skips a conflicted page and dropping it would strand the resolution. Audit 2026-08-06 N6.

entries.title: Advanced Logseq queries bind :inputs [:current-page] positionally without weakening typed date inputs
entries.notes: OG source at 6e7afa8eb040686ff057156ee877193b581dd369 resolves the typed :current-page keyword positionally through current-page-fn and lowercases the page name before query execution. Tine now retains typed AdvancedInput::Date values while binding that one keyword as AdvancedInput::Page, then conservatively lowers only the exact standard [?p :block/name ?current-page] identity joined to one [?b :block/refs ?p] or [?b :block/page ?p] relationship. Ambiguous and unrelated patterns remain visibly unsupported; this does not claim full DataScript joins. Contract-doc delta: none; this is a bounded compatibility extension within the existing partial advanced-query contract.

entries.title: Advanced queries written with block attribute patterns (:block/marker, :block/scheduled, the block's journal page) return the blocks Logseq returns, and never a narrowed answer from a partly understood not/or
entries.notes: GH #542 (bgzo, macOS 0.6.982). The advanced lowerer understood only rule heads such as (task ?b ...) and refused every DataScript attribute pattern, so [?b :block/marker "TODO"] -- also Tine's own screenshot fixture -- rendered as unsupported. Worse, a not/or containing a clause it did not understand ran as the part it did: (not [?b :block/scheduled ?d]) was dropped and the OVERDUE query returned scheduled tasks, and a partly understood not can hide blocks the query keeps. Fix (query/advanced_patterns.rs): patterns on the :find variable's marker/priority/scheduled/deadline and on its page's journal?/journal-day lower to typed filters, alone, as literals, or as a value variable narrowed by contains?/=/not=/</<=/>/>= against a literal or an :inputs date; (not [pattern]) whose variable is local to the not; single-branch or/or-join and nested and are opened. A value variable used anywhere else (a join) is not lowered. A not/or that loses any child is dropped whole, so a partial answer is only ever a disclosed superset; (not A B) now means not(A and B) rather than not(A). :result-transform is reported as not run. Fail-before: both model tests fail on the old code (first query unsupported; partial not narrowed). Out of scope: rendering config.edn :default-queries on the Journals page (not implemented in Tine at all; product decision), running :result-transform functions (ADR 0042), and the reporter's NEXT query as written, which pulls ?b while every clause binds ?h and is refused by Logseq too. Contract-doc delta: none; a bounded extension of the documented partial advanced-query subset (BACKLOG 'Advanced Datalog queries').

entries.title: The graph home page round-trips through Logseq-compatible config.edn without replacing other default-home keys
entries.notes: Config.default_home reads only the direct :page entry inside Logseq's :default-home map. Graph::set_default_home_page uses the existing guarded atomic config boundary, preserves sibling keys such as :sidebar, and refuses a malformed/non-map owner without changing its bytes. The frontend gives graph metadata precedence; when no valid graph-owned page exists it attempts to copy the old home.page.<root> app setting, deleting that legacy value only after the graph write succeeds. A refused migration remains usable for the current session and is retried later. Contract-doc delta: none; ADR 0004 and ADR 0049 already establish config.edn as the compatible graph owner outside the managed oplog domain.

entries.title: Undo cannot replay a snapshot recorded against a page instance that was evicted and re-opened

tests: src/store.test.ts::working-set eviction::refuses an undo entry recorded before the page was evicted (GH #305)

entries.notes: Working-set eviction keeps undo history by design, but the kept entry describes the evicted instance. Re-opening installs a fresh instance carrying the file's current content, and invalidateUndoForPage only runs when a load REPLACES a page that is still present, so the stale entry stayed eligible. Replaying it restored pre-eviction content and marked the page dirty; the next save submitted that content under the fresh instance's baseline, which the base-revision guard accepts because the baseline genuinely matches disk, so no conflict was ever raised. Undo/redo entries now carry the page-instance generations they were recorded against and are refused (with the page's history dropped and a toast) when any of those instances is gone. Verified fail-before: the structural-edit repro restored ['keep me','delete me'] over the external content on the unfixed tree.

entries.title: Images and streamed media can be read from nested assets directories
entries.notes: The frontend already reduced ./assets/dir/file.png to the assets-relative name dir/file.png, but all native read entry points applied the top-level-only validator used by asset creation. Read paths now accept ordinary nested relative components and retain canonical containment beneath the approved assets root. Absolute paths, empty/dot/parent components, portable backslash traversal and symlink escapes remain refused. Asset creation/import still accepts only a top-level filename.

entries.title: Opening a large Direct Files graph does not synchronously scan its pages or assets
entries.notes: The reporter measured 44.9 seconds inside the frontend load_graph call on Windows for about 13,000 pages and 25,884 files / 24.6 GB. The representative release benchmark creates 13,000 Markdown pages plus 12,884 sparse assets in 281 buckets (25.2 GiB apparent assets): current core open took 0.4 ms and the full current Linux app returned from load_graph in 65 ms; the released v0.6.90 Linux AppImage returned in 26 ms on the same fixture. Graph size alone therefore did not reproduce the Windows report. The frontend nevertheless performed two optional page-discovery operations synchronously after native binding: default-journal template discovery and configured-home-page lookup. Those may cold-scan a Direct graph and are unnecessary for first interaction. Visible Journals now owns and awaits template materialization before its first feed fetch, preserving #73, while graph open no longer duplicates that work. Configured-home lookup runs in the background and may navigate only if graph, epoch, and landing route are unchanged, so a slow result cannot override user navigation. Frontend phase logs now distinguish native binding, session restoration, and interactivity; native debug logs retain the lower-level phase timings. The Windows scenario and reporter retest remain valuable platform evidence, but the demonstrated synchronous graph-size-dependent frontend work is now removed and its ordering contracts are covered.

entries.title: Move up and down crosses child-list edges like Logseq on Android and desktop

tests: src/store.test.ts::cross-day move (journal feed as one list)

entries.notes: Tine's mobile toolbar and desktop editor command already dispatched the same moveBlockFeed operation, but that operation only swapped siblings and stopped at every nested child-list edge. OG uses one shared move-up/down handler too. Its outliner rule swaps ordinary siblings; at a boundary, moving the last child down enters the next parent sibling as its first child, and moving that first child up enters the previous parent sibling as its last child. Tine now implements that same reversible structural rule while retaining root-level journal-feed crossing, subtree identity, inherited list-style semantics, caret-preserving keyed DOM movement, and one undo unit. The regression covers both directions, a child subtree, ordinary sibling movement with Undo/Redo, and the true top boundary.

entries.title: Renaming a page onto an existing page offers the Logseq-compatible complete merge
entries.notes: The previous Tine title editor sent every edit through ordinary rename, whose correct collision guard surfaced only a backend error. OG instead asks whether to merge. The parity behavior is broader than appending two files: Cancel mutates nothing; confirmation appends the source outline after the destination, retains non-conflicting Markdown page properties, rewrites references in the source, destination and every external referrer, renames source namespace descendants to the destination namespace, removes the source, refreshes all open editor state and navigates to the destination. Managed Storage composes the SQLite-indexed exact referrer plan, descendant renames, destination edit and source deletion into one semantic transaction. Direct Files commits the recoverable source-to-trash merge before invoking its existing transactional graph-wide rename/ref rewrite, so a later failure cannot lose either page's bytes. Duplicate-journal merge remains unchanged and never rewrites page identities. Catalog maintenance 2026-08-21: references to deleted pre-0.7 runtime-oracle files were removed. Remaining or replacement references name the current clean-runtime semantic contract; the retired implementation is not accepted as release evidence.

entries.title: A fresh checkout has no tracked paths that collide on a case-insensitive filesystem
entries.notes: docs/UI-REGRESSION-TESTING.md is the current referenced execution contract; the case-only lowercase twin was an older planning document with no references and caused Git to omit one file on Windows checkout. The obsolete twin is removed, and the release-pipeline contract now folds every tracked path through NFC plus lowercase and refuses future collisions.

entries.title: Editing one block does not rewrite bytes belonging to blocks the user never touched
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 3, reproduced and re-measured independently: editing one block and reverting it failed to restore the bytes of 96 of 983 files (9.8%) on a copy of ~/research/logseq-anonymized. 88 of the 96 were an unbulleted page-level '## Heading' gaining a '- ' prefix; the worst shape injected the source layout whitespace ('\t  ') into the block TEXT and added a nesting level. Root cause was not the parser: doc.rs's source-layout retention machinery existed but every production call site passed an empty StructuralLayoutIdentity slice, so identity_bound_unbulleted_headings was always empty and the retention was inert on the Direct save path (test-only). doc::layout_identities_of now reads the locator->identity map off the document tree and serialize_page_dto_for_path passes it. Corpus after the fix: 96 damaged -> 0; unchanged-save no-op still byte-exact at 1045/0. Residual, backlogged: a whitespace-only separator line normalises to empty, which is why the continuation-heading test asserts text and depth rather than exact bytes.

entries.title: A content-only save keeps the physical page inventory warm instead of forcing a whole-graph re-read
entries.notes: Direct Files perf audit 2026-08-09, F1, found independently by both the Opus and Codex lanes with agreeing numbers (243 ms vs 263-281 ms). list_pages is memoized on raw cache_gen and its only rebuild path walks the graph text scope, re-reads every file and re-parses each one: ~35 us/file, linear from 506 to 8,006 pages, and find_entry rebuilds straight from it. Every save bumped the generation, so the first navigation or [[ autocomplete after any typing pause stalled ~1/4 s on a real 5,225-file graph. page_list_cache is now re-tagged to the new generation under the same condition the effective-identity index already uses. DELIBERATELY NARROWER than the auditor's recommendation: list_pages parses every file so a title:: edit really does move an entry (hence the !identity_changed gate), and referenced_page_names is genuinely content-derived and is left to rebuild. The test asserts a ratio, not an absolute time, so it survives a loaded shared box.

entries.title: A reference lookup overlapping an ordinary edit waits for its queued one-page SQLite delta instead of scanning the whole graph
entries.notes: GH #400 reported Unlinked References taking one to ten seconds. Direct Files already had a disposable SQLite candidate projection, but every one-page cache publication advanced the parser generation and marked SQLite unavailable until its worker applied the queued delta. A reference request in that short interval immediately used the exact but graph-wide parser fallback. The regression pauses that worker boundary and requires the read to remain pending until the bounded delta converges, while unavailable or failed projections retain the parser fallback. The separate conflict.save_baseline_present event in the report remains an intentional no-write guard for bytes that differ from the editor's loaded revision.

entries.title: Pending edits are written when the app is backgrounded or hidden, not only on a clean window close
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 7. The ONLY durability barrier in the app was onCloseRequested. Android/iOS never send one - the OS backgrounds the app and reclaims it later - so everything inside the 400ms save debounce was RAM-only. The three pre-existing visibilitychange listeners (Page.tsx, journal.ts, assetRefresh.ts) all act on becoming VISIBLE; this is the other edge. FAIL-BEFORE is an absence, not a wrong value: no listener flushed on hide, verified by grep across the tree, so there is no pre-fix test that can fail. Confidence for #255 is therefore MODERATE, not high: this is the plainest explanation for the Android half and is a real missing handler, but no same-platform reproduction of the reporter's loss exists. Findings 2 and 6 are other live candidates for the same report.

entries.title: A dirty page name with no page behind it no longer wedges every later flush
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 6. doSave bailed on a null DTO BEFORE dirty.delete(name), so the name stayed dirty forever and flushAll() could never return true again: every graph switch aborted with 'Some pages couldn't be saved' and every window close offered to discard edits that were already on disk. Reachable because pinnedPages() did not pin in-flight saves - doSave removes a page from dirty before awaiting, so the working-set cap could evict it mid-write, and a transient failure then re-added a name with no page. Two parts: savingPages() is now pinned (prevents the eviction outright), and a dirty name with no page in the store is dropped rather than wedging. Deliberately NOT dropped when the page exists but the page-header firewall refused the DTO - that is a real unsaved edit and must keep blocking.

entries.title: A watcher-driven disk reload re-checks safety at the moment it applies, not before its IPC
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 5. reloadDisposition is correct, but all four watcher sites read its verdict and then awaited backend().getPage(...) before acting - tens to hundreds of ms on a large graph, and a Syncthing burst fires many concurrently. Text typed inside that window was destroyed: upsertPage replaced the page, dropping the edit AND its undo history, with no conflict raised and nothing written to disk. store.upsertUnlessDirty already re-checked at the moment of the upsert; only these sites skipped it. reloadPageIfStillSafe re-checks centrally so a fifth watcher site cannot reintroduce the hole. reloadPage itself is deliberately left as a clobber - 'use disk version' is an explicit user decision.

entries.title: Deleting a page does its graph-wide work on the blocking pool, not the command thread
entries.notes: Direct Files perf audit 2026-08-09, F3. delete_page re-derives the page inventory and rebuilds three O(pages) indexes: measured ~95 us/file, linear, 757 ms at 8,006 files and ~1.9 s projected at 20,000. It was the only such command still running synchronously on the command thread; get_page, save_page and rename_page already cross the blocking pool. The guard test expensive_reference_and_rename_commands_cross_the_blocking_pool existed and simply did not list delete_page - a coverage omission, not a missing mechanism. This does not make delete faster; it stops it freezing command dispatch. The O(graph) cost itself is a separate, still-open finding.

entries.title: An ordinary save after an external atomic replacement compares bytes instead of refusing on physical identity
entries.notes: GH #254 increment 1, ordinary save only. An external editor that writes by temp+rename (the common safe pattern, and what Syncthing/Dropbox deliver) leaves the same path on a NEW inode. save_page authorized with PinnedSaveAuthority::LoadedRevision, whose retained-identity check refused before the byte comparison ever ran, returning 'path-pinned page does not match its captured exact owner' - a message isRetryableSaveFailure retries forever, so the page became permanently unsaveable with no user-resolvable path out. Measured pre-fix: 4 of 5 cases fail, and NOTABLY the different-byte case failed with the same unresolvable code, so a genuine external change was equally unrecoverable, not just the same-byte one. A new authority OrdinaryEditorSave proves exact path ownership and nothing about physical identity; the byte comparison then decides. Equal bytes on a new inode re-pin to the current snapshot and proceed; different bytes return the literal 'conflict' the frontend can resolve. LoadedRevision is UNCHANGED and still used by verify_existing_journal_page_projection, which authenticates before an opaque durable append and must not inherit this reorder - the contract verifier rejected a helper-wide change twice on exactly this boundary. At increment 1, delete conflicts and the force-save half were deliberately deferred to increment 2; the next record covers both.

entries.title: Keep mine writes only over the exact disk snapshot shown by its conflict
entries.notes: GH #254 increment 2. A conflict now mints one per-Graph, per-editor-episode, exact-path, monotonic-epoch token holding Present { revision, resource_identity } or Absent plus the coherently observed baseline bytes. Force consumes it before every attempt and runs the ordinary save protocol with those bytes and identity substituted as its rechecked baseline; it never delegates by revision alone. Under Martin's state-not-events ruling (2026-08-09) a byte-identical republication of the shown snapshot is a no-op, so force DOES rebind to the live inode in exactly that case and refuses a different-byte winner on a new inode; two tests pin both halves. S1-S9 each have a deterministic site test, including both final-reread arms and post-restore/post-publication observation timing. Stable observations get per-site conflict.* codes; exceptional observation failure gets conflict_retry.*, which cannot reach the keep-mine/use-disk banner and now also RETRACTS an existing one: a force has already spent its token by then, so leaving the banner up left Keep-mine permanently dead beside a destructive Use-disk (adversarial implementation verification, finding 3). Loads, watcher observations, forget_file, successful saves, and the shared Tine-owned graph-text mutation boundary revoke authority, covering rename/delete/trash/merge, managed projection/import/migration, sync-conflict resolution, and PDF-highlight page writes. Hard admission refusals remain tokenless.

entries.title: Unlinked References finds a page name written inside code, math and other literal text
entries.notes: Logseq matches unlinked references with a raw regex over the whole block content (db/model.cljs get-page-unlinked-references, only drawer/remove-logbook stripped), so code fences, inline code, math, raw HTML, examples, latex environments and hiccup are all searched. Tine derived its search region from an ALLOWLIST of block kinds in reference_evidence walk_blocks, whose `_ => {}` arm silently dropped every other variant - so the region lost coverage each time lsdoc grew a block type. Now derived by SUBTRACTION: plain_search_ranges takes the complement of what the parser already claimed (explicit refs, block refs, structural properties, :LOGBOOK: drawers), which is Logseq's own semantics reached through the parser rather than a second scanner - alias/NFC/boundary logic unchanged and new lsdoc variants covered for free. Logseq's `#`/doubled-`[` prefix rule had to be ported explicitly (og_prefix_allows): it used to be implied by overlap with a parsed reference, but inside a fence there is no parsed reference, so `[[Page]]` in code would otherwise have matched. That also corrected an inversion - for `\[[Target]]` Tine reported the escaped bracket and hid both code mentions, exactly backwards from Logseq. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, named: structural id::/collapsed::/logseq.* property text stays withheld (Logseq scans it) because a page named after a uuid fragment is not a real outcome. PERF: widening the region cost +13% (285->325 ms cold on the 1,045-file anonymized graph), so an ASCII prefilter was added to visit_plain_matches - it skips a start position only when BOTH the name's first char and the source char are ASCII, where lowercase is exact and NFC is identity, leaving folding cases like the Kelvin sign to the authoritative matcher. Net 285 ms -> 36 ms, ~8x faster than before the change. Reusing string buffers instead was measured WORSE (400 ms) because flat_map(char::to_lowercase) loses str::to_lowercase's ASCII fast path. Necessity: 6 unit tests and 2 of 3 integration tests fail on the pre-fix tree; the third asserts the complement did NOT over-widen (an explicit link and a CLOCK: line stay out) and passes both sides.

entries.title: A link naming no existing page is visibly distinguished, and a fileless #tag is not
entries.notes: Martin, 2026-08-09: a generated graph wrote each report to `pages/c01 Swap Bribery.md` with `title:: Swap Bribery` and linked the index by FILENAME. Since Logseq resolves a page's name as title:: > filename > first block (graph-parser extract.cljc get-page-name), the filename named nothing and all 29 links opened blank pages with no signal. Tine <=0.6.5 used the filename and ignored title::; aa4a4b29 (2026-07-29, shipped in 0.6.90) corrected that, which is why the graph looked fine when built. Backend was never at fault - load_named returned full content for all 30 pages. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, approved by Martin: Logseq does NOT distinguish unresolved links (components/block.cljs:548 dims only untitled-page?, i.e. a page that EXISTS under a uuid name); Tine dims them, as Obsidian does. Applied to [[refs]] only, NOT #tags - a tag with no page file is ordinary Logseq usage and dimming those would mark most tags in a normal graph. existing_page_names resolves like load_named (normalized keys + alias table, no PageKind filter, so a link to an existing journal is alive) and costs one memoized page-list read per call; pageExistsBatch coalesces every reference in a tick into one IPC, asks each name once per graph, and treats UNKNOWN AS ALIVE so a page of good links never flashes as dead. Verified on the real 30-page graph: 8/8 refs dimmed before the repair, 0/8 after, all six sampled links clicking through to 24-27 block pages.

entries.title: A fluent typing burst is never written to disk until the typist pauses
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 9. scheduleSave cleared and re-armed a 400 ms timer on every markDirty, with no ceiling, so the debounce fired only during a pause in typing. Measured fail-before: 40 keystrokes at 300 ms intervals - 12 seconds of prose at a pace slower than most people type - produced ZERO writes. A crash, power loss or OOM kill during a long passage therefore lost the whole passage, and the loss window grew with how well the writing was going. Fixed by measuring a MAX_SAVE_DELAY_MS ceiling of 3 s from the FIRST dirty mark of a burst rather than the last, so the bound is on file staleness rather than typing speed; the burst clock restarts whenever no save is armed, which every drain path (flushAll, resetSaveState, the timer itself) already guarantees by nulling saveTimer. Coalescing is unchanged: a short burst still costs exactly one write.

entries.title: "Use disk version" on a page pinned to a specific file loads a different file
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 10. Two files can carry one page NAME - the duplicate-day stray of GH #21, or same-titled pages in different folders - and the editor pins such a page to its exact path so saves write back to the file it was loaded from. ConflictBar's "Use disk version" resolved by NAME (backend getPage), which reaches the backend's canonical owner of that name, so the button silently re-pointed the tab at a different file: the user discarded their edits to THIS file and got someone else's file loaded in its place. Fixed by resolving through getPageByPath whenever the loaded page carries a path - the same idiom store.ts, RightSidebar and LiveRefGroup already use. An absent pinned file drops the page rather than falling back to the name, since that fallback is the same defect; an unpinned (never-saved) page still resolves by name because it has nothing else. needs-revalidation 2026-09-15: its cited tests were deleted with the Managed Storage removal; the Direct Files outcome still needs its own proof.

entries.title: Deleting a page with unsaved edits promises a recoverable trash copy that does not contain them
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 18. The delete confirmation said only 'The file moves to the graph's .tine-trash folder', which reads as fully recoverable. The trash receives the FILE, so a dirty page's latest keystrokes - and, provably, EVERY edit on a conflicted page, whose saves are refused by design until the conflict is resolved - are destroyed with nothing to recover from. The prompt now names that outcome when the page is dirty or conflicted, while the user can still answer no; wording is unchanged for a page with nothing unsaved. Deliberately NOT fixed by flushing first: making delete trigger a save is a behavior change with its own risk, and it cannot help the conflicted case at all.

entries.title: Closing offers to discard work that is still being written
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 11. The shared close transaction (desktop window-close and Android root Back) bounded flushAll at a flat 4 s and treated expiry as failure, so a flush that had merely not FINISHED was reported in the same words as one that could never succeed - 'unsaved changes that couldn't be saved... close anyway and lose them?' - inviting the user to throw away a write in progress. A slow or network filesystem, a fsync behind a busy disk, or many dirty pages can exceed 4 s with nothing wrong; on the 1,045-file anonymized corpus a save averages ~7 ms, so the bound is already several hundred pages' worth. The close now races the SAME flush promise twice: at the soft bound it says 'still saving' and grants a 26 s grace period, and only a flush that genuinely finished false, threw, or outlasted the grace period reaches a discard prompt - which now distinguishes 'failed' from 'still-saving' in its wording. The pre-existing test asserted that the timeout case behaved identically to failure, i.e. it encoded the defect; it was split rather than grandfathered.

entries.title: A conflict raised by a transient file removal is never cleared when the file returns
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 17. Raising a conflict was gated on a per-page divergence proof; clearing one was gated on nothing, because only a user's click (or forgetPage) ever cleared a conflict. handleGraphChange's REMOVED branch calls markConflict with no proof at all, so an external editor writing by temp+rename, or a mid-delivery Syncthing pass, could park a page behind the banner permanently. doSave then refuses that page forever, and both banner buttons destroy something: 'Use disk version' the unsaved edit, 'Keep mine' a file it never needed to overwrite. Fixed by making the proof two-directional in ONE owner, applyDivergenceVerdict, used by both observation sites (legacy watcher and sparse-v2 epoch): a negative proof on a currently-conflicted page clears the conflict and reschedules the edit it was freezing. A third site cannot reintroduce the asymmetry. A file that returns with DIFFERENT content still conflicts.

entries.title: The direct shadow-journal rule asked two extensions while its managed twin asked three
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 15, landed as a CONSISTENCY fix with an explicit NEGATIVE result. Graph::is_shadow_journal (direct mode) hard-coded canonical candidates '{stem}.md' and '{stem}.org'; its managed twin is_shadow_journal_under_permit already asked configured_text_variant_paths, i.e. all of LOGSEQ_TEXT_EXTENSIONS = md/markdown/org. The audit predicted that in a '.markdown' graph a title-named leftover would therefore escape the #21 shadow rule and poison the (kind,name) cache. IT DOES NOT: probes at the observation boundary show load_named and journals_desc both still serve the canonical file for both extensions, because later layers mask the misclassification. The necessity gate is therefore NOT satisfied and no user-visible defect is claimed - the divergence between the two classifiers is real and was removed, and the three new tests pin the #21 rule per extension so that a change in whichever layer is currently masking it cannot silently take the guarantee with it.

entries.title: The All Pages sidebar list scanned the whole page list once per visible row
entries.notes: Direct Files performance audit 2026-08-09, finding F9. pageListLabel disambiguates a row whose display name collides with another page (same title in different folders, or the same stem as .md and .org) by scanning the whole list twice - once for the name, once for the parent sub-path. The sidebar called it per rendered row, so rendering All Pages cost O(rows x pages): measured 21 ms at 5,000 pages and 39 ms at 20,000, for 300 visible rows. pageListLabels now counts both keys in ONE pass and returns a lookup, memoized in Sidebar alongside the existing filter+sort memo. The label RULE is unchanged and the three original correctness tests still pass verbatim. Necessity: the shape tests COUNT element reads through a Proxy rather than timing anything - a linear implementation reads the array once while building the index and never again, a per-row scan reads it once more per row - and both fail against the pre-fix implementation. A first attempt asserted wall-clock and was replaced after it flaked on a loaded box: 47 ms against a 26 ms ceiling with the fix in place. The index is keyed by value, not object identity, so a caller holding a copy of an entry gets the same label.

entries.title: Tine crashes at launch with a backtrace when the app-data home is not writable
entries.notes: Found while working the 2026-08-09 Direct Files audit backlog; reproduced on the stock deployed release binary, so not a regression from that work. Tauri creates the WebView user-data directory ($XDG_DATA_HOME/page.tine.Tine) inside its OWN setup(), while building the configured windows (tauri::manager::webview calls create_dir_all there), and an IO error at that point is unreachable by the application: it panics with 'Failed to setup app: Permission denied (os error 13)' at tauri-2.11.2/src/app.rs:1417, before Tine's setup hook runs. A user whose ~/.local/share is root-owned - the shape of the box this was found on, drwxr-xr-t root root - therefore got a hard crash with a backtrace and no actionable message, made more confusing by Tine's own desktop-identity step logging the same Permission denied and explicitly treating it as NON-fatal one line earlier. data_home::ensure_usable now probes the directory before anything resolves it (create_dir_all is not the question: it succeeds on an existing directory nobody may write) and, when it is unusable, points XDG_DATA_HOME at the first writable fallback for that launch - ~/.tine-data, then $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tine-data, then a uid-namespaced temp dir - so settings, session and the WebView store live somewhere real. XDG_DATA_HOME is the one lever that redirects Tauri's path resolver, WebKitGTK's website-data manager and Tine's own settings together. The frontend toasts once, stickily, naming the directory, because a silent relocation is its own defect. If nothing at all is writable the app prints one actionable sentence and exits 1 rather than panicking. Verified on the built binary: unwritable base -> app stays up, ~/.tine-data/page.tine.Tine populated with tine-settings.json and the WebKit store, nothing written to the read-only base; ordinary writable base -> no relocation diagnostic at all and no probe residue.

entries.title: A graph whose watch() failed stays blind to external changes while another graph is watched
entries.notes: Direct Files data-safety audit 2026-08-09, finding 16, landed in its REACHABLE form only. The audit claimed an inotify watch() failure leaves the watcher permanently blind with no poll fallback; that is not what the code does. A failed root is never inserted into `watched` and is retried on the next cycle, and when EVERY root fails `watched` is empty, which takes the else branch and its bounded <=3 s recv_timeout - a working recovery loop. The reachable case is mixed: with two graphs open, the inotify branch blocks on rx.recv() until an event arrives from a root that IS watched, so a root the kernel refused is retried only when some other graph happens to change. inotify limits are per-user (fs.inotify.max_user_watches), so opening a second large graph is exactly how one root fails while the other is healthy, and on a quiet healthy graph the failing one stays invisible indefinitely. inotify_cycle_wait now bounds the wait to UNWATCHED_ROOT_RETRY (3 s, matching the poll branch ceiling) whenever a desired root is unwatched, and never delays a sooner scheduled retry. Coverage gaps stated in the tests themselves: they pin the wait policy, not a real kernel watch() failure (which needs privileges unavailable here) and not the call-site wiring, and they are a specification rather than fail-before evidence because the function is new.

entries.title: Every typing lull shipped the whole reference-name inventory across IPC
entries.notes: Direct Files performance audit 2026-08-09, finding F7. The frontend's reference-name resource is keyed on dataRev, which a save bumps ~700 ms after every typing lull, so referenced_page_names ran and its result crossed IPC on every pause in typing: measured 15-23 ms and about 5,000 names at 5,225 files, with the JSON parse landing on the UI thread. The answer almost never changes, because typing inside a block rarely adds or removes a [[link]]. referenced_page_names now takes the digest of the set the caller already holds and omits the payload when it still matches, so the ordinary case is an integer. The digest is a commutative fold with the length mixed in: the memo's order comes from a HashMap, so a sequence-dependent hash would report a change on every rebuild and the gate would save nothing. NOT fixed here: the whole-graph recompute itself still runs once per cache generation, because computing the digest needs the names; making it incremental needs per-name reference counts in cache_upsert/cache_remove and is a separate packet. The frontend test pins the dangerous reading of an omitted payload - treating it as an empty set would erase every reference-only page from autocomplete and the namespace tree - and that the digest is actually presented back.

entries.title: Every save case-folded and NFC-normalised every filename in the target's directory
entries.notes: Direct Files performance audit 2026-08-09, finding F6. validate_graph_text_portable_aliases_path_local enumerates each path component's directory looking for case/NFC aliases of the target, and built a PortablePathKey for EVERY entry - a String allocation plus NFD -> default case fold -> NFC per filename. The audit's controlled experiment held graph size constant and varied only layout: 4.87 ms/save with 4,000 pages in one directory versus 0.70 ms with 40 per subdirectory, i.e. 6.9x on layout alone, growing without bound on the one directory that only ever grows (journals/) and running inside the identity-mutation lock. PortablePathKey::graph_text_components_match answers the same question without building either key when both sides are ASCII, where NFD/NFC are the identity and default case folding is exactly ASCII lowercasing. Controlled A/B on this box, same graph and build, 4,000 pages in one directory, 60 saves x 3 runs: 2.54-2.67 ms median before, 1.39-1.41 ms after (~1.8x). The both-sides-ASCII guard is load-bearing rather than redundant: folding can PRODUCE ASCII from non-ASCII (U+212A KELVIN SIGN folds to k, U+FB01 to fi), so a non-ASCII name can legitimately collide with an ASCII one and must still take the full fold. This is an identity boundary whose failure mode is admitting a collision, so the test asserts agreement with the full fold over every ordered pair of a name set that includes NFC/NFD twins, the sharp s, Cyrillic, and both fold-to-ASCII traps. Residual NOT fixed: the directory enumeration is still O(entries); removing that needs the maintained admission index to become the authority for this check, which is a data-safety boundary change and its own packet. needs-revalidation 2026-09-15: its cited tests were deleted with the Managed Storage removal; the Direct Files outcome still needs its own proof.

entries.title: A duplicated "Keep mine" spent authority minted for a newer winner nobody was shown
entries.notes: GH #254 increment 2, adversarial implementation verification finding 1 (CRITICAL) and the reachable half of finding 2. A force request named its authority only by path plus loaded revision, so consume_conflict_authority could only check SELF-consistency - that the live token is the newest - never that the user had seen it. Reachable data loss with no malicious writer: an external editor or sync client publishes B after the banner showed A; two force requests are in flight under that one banner (the button is not disabled while its request is pending) and the per-page save queue serializes them; the first correctly refuses B and, being a coherent observation, mints fresh authority FOR B; the second, issued before B existed, consumed it and overwrote B. A conflict error now carries the observation epoch it minted at, direct_save_error_message emits it as 'conflict:<n>', the frontend stores it with the banner and echoes it back on force, and consumption requires the presented epoch to equal the live token's. Found while fixing: checking ownership AFTER taking would let one stray duplicate click disarm the banner permanently, so a mis-addressed override is now refused WITHOUT spending the live token - covered by its own test. A force that can name no observation is refused at the command boundary rather than allowed to consume whatever is current. Necessity: all three new core tests fail against the pre-fix check.

entries.title: Unsaved edits were destroyed when a same-named file at a different path was loaded
entries.notes: GH #254 increment 3, contract rule 2. ensurePageLoaded replaced the loaded instance whenever the requested path differed from the incumbent's, with no check that the incumbent held unsaved work. Reproduced: the incumbent's nodes are purged, the dirty mark SURVIVES and now belongs to the replacement's content, and a live conflict banner survives describing a file the editor no longer holds. The gate is the existing reloadDisposition predicate AND an empty editor-lease set - enumerating dirty/conflicted/saving kept losing, because IME composition holds text in the textarea until compositionend and the page-title rename holds its draft in component-local signals, so neither is visible to any store predicate. A component holding uncommitted input now declares itself with a lease keyed by a unique per-component handle, released idempotently from the component lifecycle rather than only from commit/cancel - a lease that outlives its component would refuse every later replacement forever. The gate is re-evaluated synchronously at the final replacement boundary because every caller awaits a backend read first and the incumbent can become dirty during that await. Necessity: both behavioural tests fail against the pre-fix code; the lease-hygiene and clean-replacement cases pass both ways by design and are not regression guards for the refusal itself.

entries.title: An external change to a page whose block is being edited (or mid block-move, or under an editor lease) is deferred and replayed when the blocking state clears, not silently dropped

tests: src/App.test.tsx::deferred replay of externally changed pages skipped mid-edit

entries.notes: reloadDisposition's "skip" (block edit / block move) and mayReplaceInstance's lease refusal correctly declined the reload but the watcher event was then dropped: backend cache fresh, visible page stale indefinitely. The declined GraphChange is now recorded and re-dispatched through handleGraphChange when onPageBecameReplaceable fires, so the disposition is re-evaluated at replay time (a page that became dirty meanwhile takes the applyDivergenceVerdict path). Fail-before: all three App.test.tsx cases fail on pre-fix code with the page stuck at its stale content. Concord P1 freshness lane.

entries.title: Returning to the window replays deferred reloads and asks the backend watcher for one full stat diff, for filesystems that deliver no event
entries.notes: Network mounts, some sync clients and a suspended app deliver no inotify edge at all, so a page could sit stale indefinitely with the watcher healthy. Returning to the window now (a) calls sweepReplaceable() -- the P1 net, for a reload deferred mid-edit whose page never announced it became replaceable because the user alt-tabbed away -- and (b) invokes rescan_graph_now, which arms one full stat diff on the watcher thread. Findings arrive as ordinary graph-changed/graph-changed-bulk events, so the disposition, divergence proof and deferred replay all apply exactly as for a live event and no caret is stolen. The rescan is throttled (1.5 s); the sweep never is. Fail-before: with refreshOnReturnToWindow's body removed, 4 of the 6 cases fail with rescanGraphNow called 0 times. Concord P5.

entries.title: The always-ask policy converts only the SILENT external-change case into an asked one, and leaves every path that already asks or defers alone
entries.notes: Obsidian 1.9.7's one user-visible conflict policy switch (landscape survey U3). Tine's only silent adoption of external bytes is L0 freshness: a loaded, clean page is replaced with the disk version. With concord_always_ask on that change is HELD and the page offers Reload from disk / Keep mine, never a modal. The gate sits AFTER the skip and conflict branches and requires disp === reload plus a loaded page, so a dirty page still gets applyDivergenceVerdict and a mid-edit page still defers through the P1 replay machinery -- proved by the third case, where a mid-edit change is deferred, not held, and is only held once the replay re-enters with the page clean. Default is OFF and the fourth case pins the unchanged silent reload. Holding is frontend-only by design: the backend cache has already adopted the bytes, so Keep mine is honest -- the next save meets the base_rev guard and raises the ordinary conflict banner, which is Obsidian's create-a-conflict mode. Fail-before: with the policy gate removed from applyExternalChange, 3 of the 4 cases fail (getPage called once, the page shows 'fresh from disk', nothing is held). Concord P5.

entries.title: Windows watcher handling stranded new-page saves after external events and Tine's own publication echoes
entries.notes: GH #366 on v0.6.94 / Windows 11 / Direct Files: creating TINE版本更新提示词 failed three times with `external graph-text changes arrived before creation publication`, then the editor became stuck dirty. Commit 416be3cb correctly made the raw Windows watcher treat ReadDirectoryChangesW `Create(Any)` and `Modify(Any)` as exact file events, but Pending::add_event independently classified the same event as unknown and scheduled a whole-graph diff. On the reporter's 13k-page graph that kept the safe external-change admission frontier raised beyond the frontend's complete 100 ms + 300 ms retry window. GH #374 on v0.6.96 was a literal negative follow-up and revoked that coverage: Tine's own newly-published journal raised the raw external-observation frontier before debounced reconciliation could recognize the self write, so an immediate second page failed with both `awaiting watcher reconciliation` and `arrived before creation publication`. Deterministic fail-before saves journal then injects its Windows `Create(Any)` echo before the second page and observes epoch 1 instead of 0. The first repair proved exact-path self echoes, but the reporter's v0.6.97 negative follow-up exposed the missing sibling: an ambiguous callback could still publish the graph-wide epoch before waiting for an in-flight writer, making that writer refuse its own creation at the final pre-publication check. The second deterministic interleaving pauses a create at that check and proves the callback frontier waits behind the resource identity authority. The repaired raw boundary omits an exact frontier only after two coherent no-follow reads match Tine's completed revision and physical file identity; ambiguous callbacks still enter ordinary debounced reconciliation, but only after an overlapping Tine publication is complete. Different external bytes and an identical-byte replacement inode both retain the barrier. External semantic owners, exact-target races, and case/NFC aliases remain fail-closed.

entries.title: Copying the multi-page Guide was interrupted by Tine's own native watcher echo
entries.notes: Literal current-master real-app fail-before reproduced the reporter's Windows v0.6.97 outcome on Linux: the first Guide page was published, its native watcher echo raised the external-change frontier, and the next Guide page failed with `external graph-text changes arrived before creation publication`, leaving no copied namespace. Guide creation used the shared atomic Direct Files primitive but bypassed the ordinary editor commit path that records exact final bytes and physical identity for self-echo recognition. Every copied page now records that receipt after a final exact reread. The whole-guide real-app probe is the semantic proof: all pages and assets are copied, links resolve, and navigation reaches the writable copied Guide.

entries.title: Ctrl+K, #, [[ and (( share candidates within each surface's designed entity pool and window; autocomplete input stays literal and stable across character swaps
entries.notes: B1 follow-up reconciliation on current master: the remaining confirmed defect from the issue timeline (autocomplete interpreting literal text as the Ctrl+K DSL, e.g. bare OR collapsing to an empty matcher) was already fixed on master by 294edbd0 (shipped v0.6.4) and stays green; this row instead pins the remaining cross-surface contract for the 医保-style report on a synthetic CJK graph (163 eligible page candidates): the page surfaces (quick_switch = the # / [[ pool, Ctrl+K's page branch) return the SAME top-12 order, the block surfaces (( picker and Ctrl+K blocks) both find all content blocks, truncation at the shared 100 window is identical and signalled only in Ctrl+K (has_more), and pools differ ONLY by design (( searches block TEXT, # / [[ search pages, Ctrl+K searches both). The character-swap ladder (1..3 chars, incl. DSL token literals like bare uppercase OR) is re-pinned at the public quick_switch/block_search_literal APIs, complementing the shipped fix's own token tests. failBefore=inferred: written after the shipped fix; the DSL rows' pre-fix failure mode is guaranteed by the shipped fix's own token tests, and the rest documents designed behavior.

entries.title: Direct Files page rename stays bounded on a 13,000-page graph
entries.notes: GH #364 reported that both title and page-menu rename failed intermittently on a roughly 13,000-page Windows Direct Files graph with `guarded graph-text identity construction failed: initial shadow peak build memory bound exceeded`. The rename transaction already held graph-text identity authority, completed one bounded no-follow inventory, rejected directory/file aliases and logical/twin destinations, locked every touched path, re-read exact bytes before each publication, and retained rollback copies. Its nested generic atomic-write and no-replace-move helpers nevertheless tried to construct a second whole-graph retained-shadow identity index. The causal fail-before injects the reporter's exact retained-shadow peak refusal and proves rename no longer consumes that builder. Transaction-local publication now repeats only exact-target, single-link, portable-path and no-clobber checks; it updates an already-warm optional index but never builds one. The hard-link witness preserves the physical-alias refusal, and the explicit release-gate probe creates 13,000 real page files, renames one page, rewrites its distant reference, preserves the file count and records elapsed time.

entries.title: Release assembly carries an experimental 32-bit Windows lane without promising updater support
entries.notes: The fail-before inventory had no i686 lane or assets. The release matrix now cross-builds MSVC i686, stages an x86 installer and portable ZIP, and deliberately leaves latest.json unchanged until a real reporter validates usefulness on old hardware.

entries.title: Production diagnostics retain bounded content-free events and exact-build decoding evidence
entries.notes: The recorder writer accepts only fixed event names, catalogued IPC command names, enums, booleans, counts and durations; detailed debug strings never enter the report. Current/previous one-MiB segments, unclean-exit marker, private files and process lock are native-tested. Release tests pin line-level symbols, hidden maps copied outside dist, exact-SHA artifact naming and removal of maps from shipped assets.

entries.title: On a web engine older than Safari 15.4 Tine says so at startup and how to fix it, instead of opening half-working with a failed parser
entries.notes: GH #572, jaemskyle: macOS Big Sur 11.7.8, 0.6.984 DMG. The system WKWebView was Safari-14-era: the lsdoc wasm failed to compile ('can't get 0th argument Type' -- the vendored module declares an externref parameter, the reference-types feature, Safari 15) and the frontend then threw on Array.prototype.at (Safari 15.4), so every page showed 'This page could not be displayed' and the block-renderer banner. Tine's declared floors were false: macOS had Tauri's default 10.13 and iOS was set to 14.0. Martin chose (2026-09-21) to require the Safari 15.4 engine with a clear message rather than support Safari 14: index.html runs an ES5 classic check (at, Object.hasOwn, structuredClone, and WebAssembly.validate of a one-type externref module) before the app module, renders the explanation and remedy (update Safari; iOS 15.4), and main.tsx stops and reveals the window on its flag. iOS minimumSystemVersion is 15.4. A source scan keeps post-15.4 built-ins out of src/. Verified in Chromium against the production build with Array.prototype.at deleted and with the reference-types probe failing: flag set, message shown, app not mounted; unmodified, the app mounts. Not verified on a real Safari 14 engine. Known limit, documented in the Guide: pdf.js needs Safari 17.4 (Promise.withResolvers, AbortSignal.any, class static blocks in the PdfViewer chunk only).

entries.title: A settings write on storage that refuses atomic no-replace renames leaves config.edn in place, and a graph already hit by it opens again
entries.notes: GH #538 (Android, 0.6.982): after a failed write, the graph never opened again with a bare 'unsafe graph layout: Invalid argument (os error 22)'. atomic_replace_expected (the config.edn writer) retired the live file with a plain rename, then published with renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE); on storage that answers the flag with EINVAL both the publish and the no-replace undo failed, the undo error was ignored, and config.edn stayed stranded under .config.edn.<pid>.<seq>.retired. The open-time restore used the same refused primitive, so every open failed. The Android flag refusal is recorded from Android CI run 32091898520; it is device-dependent and was not reproduced on the reporter's device. Fix: prove the no-replace move on the staged temp before retiring the live name (refusal leaves config.edn untouched, with a named error); restore a vacated name by plain rename only when the storage refuses the flag AND the target is absent; name the step and file on recovery errors. Tests gh538_* inject an EINVAL mover; 3 of 4 fail on the old logic (the fourth covers error wording). Not covered: Direct page saves on such storage still fail (named error), a separate decision.

entries.title: Reopening a graph whose search index is current does not rebuild the index because the Journals feed read pages before the warm
entries.notes: GH #550 (Android, 764 pages, ~40 s open on every launch). The Journals feed loads its first days before the warm has validated the reopened projection; each load_page published a Replace delta, and the cold queue numbered those pages 0,1,2,... while the image already stored other pages at those positions. The delta turn failed with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: pages.position', the projection went stale, and the warm rebuilt all of it -- every launch. Where the positions happened to line up, the feed pages were still re-lowered for nothing. Fix: before an inventory seeds the session's page order a delta carries no position; the worker drops pre-seed deltas whose page the image holds at the same source revision, applies changed ones in place (storage keeps their stored position), and hands a page the image does not hold to the warm's fresh build. Tests: gh550_journal_feed_before_the_warm_keeps_a_clean_reopen_clean fails deterministically on the old code (projection failure on drain; 3 needless re-lowerings when positions line up); gh550_launch_reads_of_changed_and_new_pages_settle_without_failing covers the changed/new siblings. Real corpus (logseq-anonymized with journals renamed to dates ending yesterday, feed's 3 days loaded before the warm): old code 'projection is stale' + 1,078 lowerings on each relaunch, fixed 0. Not measured on the reporter's phone.

entries.title: Opening today's journal at launch does not first enumerate every file in the graph
entries.notes: GH #550 launch-cost follow-up. get_page for a journal title went through find_entry, whose miss on a cold cache enumerated the whole graph inventory before loading one file (most of an 8 s get_page on the reporter's phone). load_named now resolves a journal title to its date-stem file (md/org variants) and loads it directly, answering only when exactly one date-stem file exists and the loaded page keys to the requested title; every other shape (title:: rename, md+org twins, title-named stray, absent day) falls back to the inventory path. gh550_todays_journal_opens_without_walking_the_graph fails on the old code (43 inventory visits for a 41-file graph; 0 with the fast path); gh550_journal_by_date_answers_what_the_inventory_lookup_answers checks the sibling shapes answer as the inventory lookup does. Same batch: the per-launch whole-graph backup no longer starts 1 s after open; it waits for the window's warm-done plus a 5 s quiet period (180 s deadline). That schedule is covered only at the policy level (gh550_launch_backup_waits_for_startup_to_go_idle); not measured on the reporter's phone.

entries.title: A non-page entry in journals/ or pages/ (symlink, unreadable sidecar, hidden hard link) no longer blanks the Journals view or refuses today's journal and renames
entries.notes: GH #385 (macOS, iCloud Drive graph): Journals showed 'No journal entries found' while All pages worked. Chain: the feed prepends an empty today placeholder; its activate_absent_editor(Journal) resolves through the configured walk of journals/+pages/, which (unlike the graph-wide inventory) refused any symlink, opened every non-page file (an unreadable .DS_Store, attachment, or refused iCloud download fails the open), and refused any two files on one inode. Since v0.6.94 loadFeed aborted the whole feed on one refused page and restartJournalFeed returned null, so the generic empty message showed and the retry loop repeated the failing call (5 activate_absent_editor failures in the reporter's diagnostic). Fix: the configured walk skips symlinks, hidden entries and non-page files before opening them (the save capture already skips symlinks since GH #267; write targets are opened no-follow); two page files on one inode are still refused. loadFeed leaves out a page whose activation failed and installs the rest; unsaved work and stale requests still defer the feed atomically. The same walk backs page rename, merge, PDF and journal migration, which are fixed too. The exact entry on the reporter's graph is not known; the test covers Emacs lock symlink, page symlink, unreadable .DS_Store and attachment, hidden hard link, hidden unparseable page name, and an iCloud placeholder. Not verified on macOS/iCloud.

entries.title: One entry the page scan cannot read (FIFO, unreadable folder or page, oddly named file) no longer leaves the graph with zero pages, every page opening blank
entries.notes: GH #332 (theaffman, Steve-21-bassman, dealingwith; Windows and Android, since after v0.6.5): graphs opened with every page blank. v0.6.90 replaced the tolerant list_md walk with the strict graph-wide inventory walk, which aborted on any entry it could not admit; the page cache was then installed with zero pages, list_pages returned [] and get_page returned 'absent', which the frontend renders as an empty new page (hence activate_absent_editor after every open in the reporters' diagnostics). The config (custom journals dir, dd-MM-yyyy) plays no part. Fix: the graph-wide READ walk skips an entry it cannot admit; an unreadable page file is recorded as a page index failure (source not complete), an unreadable folder or non-page entry is skipped without one. The configured walk (writes) and inventory limits stay fail-closed. Separately, list_sync_conflicts and list_vcs_marker_conflicts read every page file as sync commands on the main thread, freezing every command for 10-16 s at startup in the reporters' diagnostics; both are now async + spawn_blocking with a source guard. Test gh332_* reproduces FIFO, non-UTF-8 image name, unreadable folder, unreadable nested page and unreadable page: pre-fix list_pages is empty. Which entry each reporter has is not known. Not addressed: Windows FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT refusal of cloud-placeholder files (OneDrive etc.), unverified here and not indicated in the thread; the empty-looking UI does not yet name page-index failures.

entries.title: The default journal template is never re-applied over text the user typed into a child block of today's journal
entries.notes: Found while tracing GH #550 (not the reporter's symptom). materializeJournalTemplate treated today's journal as empty when every TOP-LEVEL block was blank. The usual template shape leaves an empty parent with children, so text typed into a child was overwritten by the template on the next launch, focus, visibility or watcher refresh. The check now looks at the whole block tree. Reproduced by the #550 investigation with a backend probe; frontend test fails before, passes after.

entries.title: With a custom journal title format, opening a graph no longer saves the journal template over an already-delivered today's journal (a spurious save conflict on every launch)
entries.notes: GH #550 diagnostics showed save_page failing with direct.save conflict.save_baseline_present about 15 s after every launch with no edit. Graph bind bumped the epoch (waking the Journals surface) before applyConfigDerivedState set the graph's journal title format, so the template lookup used the default 'MMM do, yyyy' title, found no page for a custom-format graph, and saved the template with no base revision; the backend's date fallback mapped it onto today's real file delivered by Syncthing, hence the conflict (or a silent create when the file was absent). The error was swallowed, so no data was lost. The title format is now set before setGraphMeta/bumpGraphEpoch at bind and on live config change. The reporter's config lines were not confirmed. The 40 s open itself is not addressed here.

entries.title: An outside change to logseq/config.edn is picked up while Tine is running, instead of being ignored until the next graph open
entries.notes: Reported by Martin 2026-08-25 while reviewing the favorites work: config.edn was read once per graph open, so a settings change made in Logseq, a text editor, or delivered by Syncthing was invisible for the rest of the session AND the next settings write from Tine was computed against the stale copy. Root cause: the OS watcher already subscribed recursively to the graph root and already classified logseq/config.edn as GraphTextExactFeedPathClass::Configuration, but incremental_page_paths discarded the path because .edn is not an eligible page extension, so nothing ever re-read the file. Fixed by queueing configuration paths separately (Pending::config_paths) and refreshing the graph when the on-disk bytes differ from those the running Graph was opened with (Graph::open_config_description vs model::config_file_description). That byte gate is mandatory, not an optimization: a refresh discards the whole page cache, and Logseq rewrites config.edn on many ordinary UI actions. The watcher never blocks on the storage transition lane (RefreshLaneWait::TryOnce, deferred and retried) because blocking would stall reconciliation for every graph behind one graph's load or promotion. Configuration is a plain filesystem file under BOTH storage engines - never in GraphTextScope, never in the oplog - so there is one mechanism, not a Direct/managed fork. Fail-before: the pre-fix Pending queue drops an exact config.edn event entirely (incremental_page_paths returns Some(vec![])), which is what the two new watcher tests assert against; before the change config_paths did not exist and the queue was empty for every writer shape. NOT CLOSED: :favorites is still written wholesale from the frontend's snapshot, so a favorite added in Logseq inside the reload window can be overwritten by the next star toggled in Tine; that needs a three-way merge in set_favorites' own atomic_update closure. ALSO FIXED HERE: src-tauri/src/sync_runtime.rs constructed a GraphMeta literal in a test and was never updated when favorites_page was added in b4847dd7, so `cargo test -p tine --lib` did not compile on master. The npm/tsc gates do not build src-tauri tests and the Rust suite compared by name was tine-core, so nothing caught it. SELF-WRITE: a settings write leaves the running graph's parsed view stale (it always has; set_favorites never refreshed it), so the byte gate alone would read every star toggled in the sidebar as an outside change. Graph::write_config is now the single funnel all 13 setters publish through and records what it wrote; the watcher accepts either the open-time digest or that marker. A managed slot retains no Graph to ask, so it re-reads unconditionally and the FRONTEND declines to re-seed favorites it is already showing - fail-before proven by forcing that guard false (the test fails). Also classified set_favorites_page in MANAGED_COMMAND_SURFACE: a third defect from b4847dd7 whose own guard test could not run because the crate did not compile.

entries.title: The flight recorder releases its single-writer lock when it is dropped, not when the last forked copy of the descriptor closes

sources.internal: Flaky first-run census 2026-09-03, finding 2

coverage.failBefore: proven — with the Drop impl removed the new test fails with the exact signature the census recorded from the real flakes: Os { code: 11, kind: WouldBlock, message: "Resource temporarily unavailable" }

entries.notes: FlightRecorder held its process.lock in a `_process_lock: File` field with no Drop and no unlock, so release was a side effect of closing that descriptor. An flock belongs to the open file description, not to the descriptor: every process spawn duplicates the description into a child that holds it until exec, so a recorder dropped inside that window left the lock held and the next open on the same directory got EAGAIN. Observed twice in campaign evidence (wave3 I5, wave4 G1) as a first-run failure of the two session-cleanliness tests that then passed on rerun — four extra `cargo test -p tine` invocations in the G1 lane alone, on the gate every lane runs. Drop now calls unlock, which acts on the description and so releases every copy at once.
