entries.title: An advanced query answered for the wrong page, or for the day it was parsed on

sources.internal: 2026-09 query-engine campaign, packet P0-rust Wave D; SPEC 4.4 (R5), CLOSURE 2; invariants I-12, I-22

entries.notes: An advanced (datalog) query whose inputs are :current-page or a relative date has no answer until it is executed: the same authored text means different things on two pages and on two days. Binding those inputs anywhere but at execution -- in the parse, or once per cache fill -- shows the reader another page's linked references, or yesterday's journal window, with no sign anything is stale. One resolver now runs before invalidity checks, normalization, cache lookup and the explain-empty decomposition: query_parse stays context-free and retains the complete authored form, and resolve_for_execution(query, context, today) lowers it through the ONE existing advanced_pred, returning the bound query plus the ran/ignored/supported report. A resolution that cannot bind an input answers with strict no results and says so in the report rather than answering with a plausible wrong set, and run, explain and export all go through the same resolver, so they cannot disagree.

entries.title: A content match answer depended on which engine ran it

sources.internal: 2026-09 query-engine campaign, packet P0-rust Wave D; SPEC 5.10 (R3), CLOSURE 4; invariants I-12, I-13

entries.notes: `content match` promises the graph search box's semantics: substring terms (so `foobar` answers `foo`, `oob` and `oo`), quoted phrases with their internal whitespace, OR arms, negated terms and an exclusion-only query. A standard word-token FTS index gets the first three wrong, so the walk and a token-index route would answer the same query differently and the user would watch results appear and disappear by route rather than by content. The leaf now carries the payload parsed ONCE by the search box's own search_query::Matcher, reached through Filter::match_sources and CompiledLeaves::match_program, so any future engine inherits that parse instead of re-deriving it; an empty or invalid-regex Match is a false leaf, including under `not`; and Match is legal only on `content`. The named fixture list -- foobar/foo/oob/oo, phrases with leading, repeated and tab or newline whitespace, whitespace-only terms, OR arms mixing short and long, negatives, exclusion-only, invalid regex, Unicode, escaped quotes -- plus every example the search help text displays is the corpus the future SQL route must reproduce row for row.

Removing a column total or a grouping in the builder cleared the properties but reprinted the directive into the text, so the next parse restored what the user had just deleted; and because precedence is unconditional, a stale text copy could also outlive a change made anywhere else. Classification: exact safety/interoperability -- the disagreement is about what the file MEANS. One question, one answer (I-12): `og_view` no longer emits `aggregate` or `group-by` at all, while `sort-by` and `sample` keep their text form because OG itself reads those, and every save now writes all SIX SPEC 7.6 view properties (`tine.view`, `tine.sort`, `tine.group-by`, `tine.fields`, `tine.col-aggregates`, `tine.sample`) under both macro names -- writing `null` for the absent ones, so a removal is persisted as an absence rather than left behind. `og_expressible` is deliberately unchanged: a query with aggregates is still OG-expressible and still stays a `{{query}}`. entries.title: The `don't show this again` choice for the query-crossing notice is device-local and graph-keyed, and never enters the graph

entries.notes: Capability with a data-safety edge: a user who ticks `Don't show this again` on the query-crossing notice must not thereby write anything into the graph, and must not have the choice follow them to another device (I-18) -- while a second graph on the same device must still get its own answer. The dismissal set is stored in app-data as `sessions/<graph_storage_key>-notices.json`, keyed exactly the way `session_path`/`workspaces_path` key theirs (D-11), and written with `tine_core::model::atomic_write` rather than `fs::write` (D-7) -- the audited-write allowance in this file moves 3 -> 4 with the new save, which is the point of that allowance being a number. Three refusals are deliberate and each names an in-scope failure: a missing file, an unreadable file and a MALFORMED file all read as `{"dismissed":[]}` and write nothing back, so a truncated or externally corrupted device file costs the user a re-shown notice and never a refused save; the next ordinary dismissal repairs it. `load_workspaces_at`'s body is NOT reused (D-3/G2): it carries a migration this store has no history to migrate, and copying it would have imported a fallback that writes on read. The frontend reads the store at most once per graph epoch, so nothing here runs on a query or keystroke path (I-13), and a store that cannot be read leaves the notice SHOWING rather than silently suppressed.

entries.notes: The baseline for what a save writes is the block's currently PERSISTED property value, never a 'user touched this control' flag. `og_view` re-emits only `(sort-by ...)` and `(sample ...)`, so a grouping or an aggregate authored in the query text is dropped by the reprint of an unrelated FILTER edit -- only a property write keeps it, and a crossing to `{{tine-query}}` (whose text carries no directives at all) therefore materializes the whole effective view in the same undo unit. A second defect surfaced while fixing: without the erase’s side effect of publishing `pending.rebuild`, two concurrent startup queries raced on the recovery lock and the loser reported the terminal “The query index could not be read”; a repair now publishes an in-flight marker that `progress_at` reports as Working(Recovering), so the losing query retries.

The user outcome is kept by a different mechanism: before the index is ready, Ctrl+K and the (( picker search one loaded parsed snapshot and rerun against the complete index when it is published; a cold or replacement build runs in an unpublished stage with one atomic publication, and edits during it reconcile afterwards instead of restarting it. entries.title: A page renamed, merged, rescued, trashed, migrated or written to a second file of the same journal day is findable as what it now is, instead of leaving search answering from what it was

sources.internal: convergence audits 3-6 on branch batch/gh543-convergence

coverage.failBefore: tine-agents/evidence/gh543-convergence/round6/necessity.log (each sixth-audit production fix reverted alone at abd0536f: A6-N1, A6-N2, A6-N3 with its class guard, A6-N4 and A6-N5 each red, the rest of the suite green) and .../round7/necessity.log (A7-N1, A7-N2 and A7-N3 the same way, A7-N3 showing page_order=2 pre-fix). Rounds 3-5 were proved the same way per fix during implementation.

entries.notes: Blocking core operation, all platforms: from v0.6.983 search answers from the SQLite projection rather than an in-memory walk, and a mutation that changed what the graph contains without publishing a producer left the index with a committed image nothing was converging. Partial admission then made the answer SUCCEED, and a successful answer never reaches the repair a refusal would start, so it never corrected itself: a rename kept offering the old name, a merge returned both pages with one of them in the trash, a rescued file was never findable, a trashed or filename-migrated journal answered twice, a path-pinned save and an externally delivered edit to a duplicate-day file reached the index never, and a migrated PDF highlight page answered from the trash. Fix: every mutation publishes through one front door - cache_upsert for a file this process rewrote, cache_remove_path for a file that left, direct_projection_publish_page_set for a multi-page set under one queue lock - the parsed whole-graph cache is treated as the authoritative producer it is (so a repair cannot republish a page a mutation removed), the journal filename migration holds the identity gate across its parse and publication, and a merge rollback compensates only when the restore actually put the file back. Class guard: a_moved_file_is_never_retired_by_a_lookup_that_can_come_back_empty fails on a retirement by name that hands over no entry. Seventh audit: `graph_text_move_noreplace` renames BEFORE its fallible durability and identity work, so an Err from it does not mean the file stayed put - the merge rollback now publishes whatever the source path actually holds afterwards, and the journal migration asks the filesystem whether each move landed, publishes the moves that did happen on every exit, and no longer reports Ok(0) for a file it moved. An unchanged redelivery of a duplicate-day file publishes nothing, matching the suppression the ordinary file path has always had.

entries.title: An operation that fails AFTER its file move already committed still leaves search describing the files that are actually on disk

coverage.failBefore: tine-agents/evidence/gh543-convergence/round8/necessity.log (each fix disabled in turn on the round-7 head 93dd3c14: the four move regressions fail on "retired source still searchable" / "search must describe the live paths", the rename regression expects ["Beta"] and observes [], the conflict regression finds no producer for the surviving occupant; all six pass with the fixes restored)

entries.notes: Blocking core operation, and the error-path half of REG-QUERY-PROJECTION-MUTATION-PUBLISHES-543. graph_text_move_noreplace performs the no-clobber rename FIRST and only then makes the chain durable and finishes identity, so an Err from it means the file HAS moved and a later step failed. Every caller that exited on that error skipped its ordinary publication: merge staging, file rescue, page deletion and journal trash each left the vanished source answering searches (rescue additionally kept returning the retired page name instead of the live one); a rename whose compensation preserved an external replacement at the destination left those real, readable bytes unindexed; and a failed duplicate-day resolution kept describing the stray text it could no longer remove. In each case the projection reported itself idle, ready and validated at generation 0 with nothing queued, so nothing was ever going to correct it - a successful search served from an image with no convergence work, which is the other half of GH #543's indexing-forever. Fix: the shared move primitive reconciles the actual eligible source and destination paths when its own post-rename work fails - readable bytes through parse_exact_page/cache_upsert, confirmed absence through cache_remove_path - and still returns the original error; rename_page and resolve_duplicate_journal_day reconcile their final edit paths after failed compensation. graph_text_move_to_trash needed no separate fix because it delegates to the same primitive. The second rename site, graph_text_move_editor_recovery_noreplace, has the same partial-commit shape but runs only inside recover_interrupted_editor_publications at graph open, before any index exists, so it cannot strand a stale image; it is deliberately not covered here.

entries.title: A save that fails after it has already changed the file still leaves search finding the text that is really on disk

coverage.failBefore: tine-agents/evidence/gh543-convergence/round10/necessity.log (the reconciliation disabled in commit_editor_write on the integrated head 2a77c84d: all three regressions fail at the live-text search assertion after their disk and error assertions pass; all three pass restored)

entries.notes: Blocking core operation, and the ordinary-save sibling of REG-QUERY-PROJECTION-FAILED-MUTATION-PUBLISHES-543 - reached far more often than a failed move, because it is the editor path every keystroke eventually takes. An editor write that changed the file and then failed propagated its error through write_page's `?` before cache_upsert, so nothing published: search went on serving the pre-save text and could not find the text now on disk, with the projection idle, ready and validated at generation 0 and nothing queued. Worse for the variant that fails after the inner commit returns: the leftover self-write marker made the FIRST checked watcher delivery a no-op (sync_file_checked returns Ok(None) because the marker matches the new bytes), and the native reconciler treats Ok(None) as success and advances its file stamp, so the one delivery that would have repaired it was consumed. Third variant: an external writer wins the path after publication, production raises conflict.replace_post_publication, and that real readable winner reached no producer either. Fix: commit_editor_write reconciles the final path through the same front door the failed-move fix uses (reconcile_failed_graph_text_paths) on every error from its commit/final-read body, clearing the marker and publishing the actual readable owner or confirmed absence, and returns the original error unchanged; the success path and the conflict/no-clobber protocol are untouched. The DTO is never published merely because its write was attempted - the external-winner regression pins that by rejecting the attempted editor text. Assertion change recorded: the two foreign_destination_* tests previously required a failed save to advance NO cache generation and to leave the stale cached document standing; that assertion was the defect written down, and they now require the surviving foreign winner's document, which still fails if the editor's own bytes are published.

entries.title: Searching a large graph reads only the blocks that can match the typed needle, instead of every block in the graph for every keystroke

sources.internal: 2026-09-17 SQL full-scan census, first item; before/after measured with read_latency_probe_reports_per_surface_timings on the 10,000-page probe graph

coverage.failBefore: tine-agents/evidence/bounded-reads/fail-before.log (bound neutralised: one matching block, but the statement ranked all 205 rows of the page; assertion "one candidate, but the statement ranked 205 rows of a 205-block page"); before/after pair from one build in tine-agents/evidence/bounded-reads/ctrl-k-before-after.md (unbounded 4372 ms zero-hit and 4524 ms at 101 hits, bounded 1677 ms and 1721 ms, both runs exit 0)

entries.notes: Blocking stateful UX on large graphs. The Friendly read scanned every block in scope TWICE per keystroke: the block-results CTE carried no content condition, and the page-by-content membership CTE carried none either, so both materialised every block, called the rank program on each, and let the outer select keep the matches. Cost did not depend on the needle. On the 10,000-page probe graph (600k blocks) the median Ctrl+K search was 4372 ms for a needle matching nothing and 4524 ms for one matching 101 blocks. The fix derives a sound candidate needle from the branch predicate (VisibleContent, Contains or Phrase, first whitespace-free run of at least 3 characters, through And but never Or/Not/Regex/Fuzzy) and makes the trigram index over search_substring_fts the DRIVING table of both reads, through one shared helper so a future third reader cannot miss it. Driving is the load-bearing part: the same index used as a WHERE-clause filter left SCAN b in the query plan and only skipped the rank call, which measured as no useful saving. Measured after: 1677 ms zero-hit, 1721 ms at 101 hits, and no needle slower than its baseline by more than run-to-run noise (worst +53 ms, ranges overlapping). Above BLOCK_CANDIDATE_CAP = 20000 candidates the helper returns the unbounded scan, because driving a 600k-row candidate set measured 2045 ms against 1246 ms scanned; the cap probe costs 0-4 ms at every selectivity because it counts with LIMIT cap+1, which a bare COUNT would not. The bound only narrows which rows are asked: the exact predicate still decides the answer in SQL and is re-checked per row in Rust, so a wrong bound shows up as a missing result rather than a wrong one. A needle too short to index, or any shape supplying none, stays unbounded and is answered exactly as before. One semantic delta: the driven path reaches blocks through the text index, so a block carrying no block_text row is omitted rather than surfaced through missing_text = 1. No search result changes, because a textless block cannot satisfy a Contains predicate; the consequence is that the Friendly corruption tripwire for that shape now fires only on the scan path. The page-content CTE is an inner join and never had that arm.

entries.title: Page-link autocomplete on a large graph answers from a remembered reference-name set instead of re-reading the whole reference index on every lookup

sources.internal: 2026-09-17 quick-switcher full-scan follow-up to REG-FRIENDLY-BLOCK-CANDIDATE-BOUND-001; before/after measured with read_latency_probe_reports_per_surface_timings on the 10,000-page probe graph

coverage.failBefore: tine-agents/evidence/quickswitch-scan/ — memo reverted with the test kept: FAILED, 0 passed; 1 failed, on the assertion that a second call at one cache generation must not re-drain the projection; restored tree: ok, 1 passed; 0 failed. Probe pair on the 10,000-page graph: before, quick_switch 1408-1430 ms flat across 8 needles and producer:referenced 1388 ms; after, 9-12 ms per needle and producer:referenced 0 ms for the same 10,010 names.

entries.notes: Blocking stateful UX on large graphs. quick_switch is NOT Ctrl+K (that is run_graph_search_latest_displayed); it backs the in-editor [[..]] page picker (limit 100, one call per debounced keystroke), the quick capture picker, the query sheet's page field and Settings. legacy_page_search_entries takes its three candidate sets BY VALUE before the needle is consulted, so the cost could not live in the match loop; a per-producer probe split the flat ~1400 ms exactly: list_pages 0 ms (10,001 entries), page_aliases_with_owners 0 ms, referenced_page_names 1388 ms. The projection answers referenced names by draining navigation_reference_names_after, whose DISTINCT spans (source_page_id, path, raw_name, normalized_name) while tine-core folds by page_key(raw_name) alone: 110,000 rows transported to yield 10,010 names, measured at 1.29 s against the real fixture. Nothing memoized it, although the sibling list_pages has had exactly this memo for exactly this reason. The fix adds referenced_names_cache keyed on cache_gen, storing the set's digest beside the names so a hit does not re-hash 10k strings, and memoizes ONLY the projection path: the parser fallback deliberately answers empty when the page cache is cold, so caching that would make 'this graph references no pages' stick for a whole generation and autocomplete would silently offer nothing. A read is memoized only if the generation still matches the one it was keyed on, so a set recorded under a stale key cannot outlive the edit that invalidated it. The memo is therefore exactly as fresh as the read it replaces, which already refuses to answer at any other generation; a save bumps cache_gen through cache_upsert_inner, so a newly linked page appears on the next lookup. Control surfaces unchanged (graph_search 1637/4516/4448/1711 ms against 1677/4601/4495/1721 baseline; search steady at 2.7-2.9 s). Two cheaper-looking alternatives were measured and REJECTED before being written: raising the cursor batch from 512 to 16384 cut statements 215 to 7 and left the time unchanged (1.293 s vs 1.352 s), because the cost is the scan and not the round trips; and a storage reader returning distinct names only measured 2.57-16.85 s, 2-13x SLOWER, because raw_name carries no index so its cursor predicate cannot seek. A covering index was investigated as the way to fix the first call too. The shape recorded here first - reference_postings(target_type, reference_kind, normalized_name, source_page_id, raw_name), credited with 1.29 s to 0.084 s - was WRONG, and the error is worth keeping: measured against the SHIPPED statement it runs 1.765 s, slower than the 1.276 s baseline, because reference_kind <= 4 is a range predicate sitting ahead of the sort keys, which costs USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY and makes the cursor statement abandon the new index entirely. The 0.084 s had been measured on a hand-written paraphrase of the reader rather than on NAVIGATION_REFERENCE_NAMES_FIRST_SQL itself. Corrected 2026-09-17: Martin authorized the forced projection rebuild while the schema is still being tuned, so tine-storage v0.24.0 takes reference_postings(normalized_name, raw_name, reference_kind) WHERE target_type = 0 TOGETHER WITH a narrower statement that drops the pages join and source_page_id, measured 1.276 s to 0.022 s (110,000 rows to 10,010) with the returned name set proven identical by set comparison. Remaining limit, stated plainly: the first lookup after any edit still pays the full drain, because a save bumps the generation. Priming the memo at generation publish was considered and rejected, since it would put a 1.4 s background drain behind every save on a large graph.

entries.title: The first page-link lookup after an edit names every linked page from a covering index instead of draining one row per page-and-spelling

sources.internal: 2026-09-17 follow-up to REG-QUICKSWITCH-REFERENCE-NAMES-MEMO-001, which fixed every repeat lookup but left the first one after each edit paying the full drain; Martin authorized the forced projection rebuild that makes an index affordable ("we are still tuning the sqlite thing; it's fine to force a rebuild at an update")

coverage.failBefore: The behaviour is proven in the pinned crate, not in this repo: the plan guard paged_navigation_readers_use_an_index_range FAILS against the pre-change statement, reporting plan ["SCAN r USING INDEX reference_postings_normalized_name_idx", "USE TEMP B-TREE FOR DISTINCT"] where it now requires SCAN/SEARCH ... USING COVERING INDEX reference_postings_navigation_names_idx. Measured on a faithful copy of the 10,000-page probe projection (1.2M postings, 1.55 GB): baseline as shipped 1.276 s; covering index alone, statement unchanged, 0.390 s; index plus dropping the pages join 0.152 s; index keyed to the DISTINCT with the join and page id dropped 0.022 s (110,000 rows in 215 statements to 10,010 in 20). Batch size stops mattering (0.022 s at both 512 and 4096), which is the proof the cost was always the scan. Name-set equality checked element-wise, not by count: 10,010 distinct raw_name both ways, zero elements on either side only. Gating runs archived at tine-agents/evidence/quickswitch-index/ (README names what each proves): 48 failures with the index unregistered on the ordinary creation path, then 3, then 1, then 218 passed and 0 failed with cargo fmt --check clean and api.txt byte-identical.

entries.notes: Blocking stateful UX on large graphs; the residue left by REG-QUICKSWITCH-REFERENCE-NAMES-MEMO-001. The memo answers every lookup within one cache generation, but a save bumps cache_gen, so the first [[ lookup after any edit re-drained the projection for ~1.3 s. Fixed in the projection rather than in tine-core: reference_postings_navigation_names_idx on (normalized_name, raw_name, reference_kind) WHERE target_type = 0, plus a statement narrowed to the DISTINCT it actually wants -- the pages join and source_page_id are dropped because the only consumer folds by page_key(raw_name) and reads no other column. The index ALONE is just 3.3x (1.276 s to 0.390 s); the win needs index and statement together. COLUMN ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: reference_kind first puts a range predicate ahead of the sort keys, costs USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY, and measures 1.765 s -- slower than no index at all, which is exactly the shape an earlier note recommended on the strength of a hand-written paraphrase of the reader; the standing lesson is to measure the literal shipped SQL constant. Cost of adoption, accepted by Martin explicitly: SQLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION 28 to 29 makes validate_graph_projection_schema (the Direct reader's schema check; validate_schema_and_claim has no caller in Tine) refuse every existing projection, so each user's first launch after the update rebuilds it once. Unit cost: the index is 88.4 MB on a 1.64 GB projection (5.4%, measured with dbstat rather than by differencing a vacuumed file -- the differencing method overstated it as +218 MB by counting free pages the VACUUM reclaimed), ~1.8 s to build, and per edit the reference_postings replacement step of a save costs +0.007 ms on a 1-posting page and +0.057 ms on a 60-posting page (interleaved A/B/A/B over 4 rounds x 60 cycles; a first non-interleaved run showed the index making saves FASTER, which is impossible, and was cache/WAL ordering noise). Registering an index in tine-storage takes NINE sites, not the seven an earlier note listed: the two it missed were the execute_batch DDL string in initialize_graph_projection_schema -- the ordinary creation path, whose omission left EXPECTED_INDEXES demanding an index nothing built and failed 48 tests with 'no such index' -- and the Direct query metadata marker in SOURCE_REVISIONS_DDL, which advances 28 to 29 so an older Direct reader, which validates that table's DDL text but tolerates extra indexes, rebuilds a newer cache instead of accepting it. api.txt needed no bless: it records the public surface at name granularity, so dropping two public fields left it byte-identical; that is not evidence the change is non-breaking, since cargo semver-checks reads rustdoc and is what forces v0.24.0. Known remaining sibling, deliberately not taken here: NAVIGATION_ALIASES_FIRST_SQL still plans a pages join plus a temp B-tree for DISTINCT and another for the last ORDER BY term. It is a follow-up, not a blocker, and page_aliases_with_owners genuinely reads owner_path, so the join may not be droppable and this fix may not transfer. One real regression was caught by the rust gate and is worth recording, because the measurement that cleared the change could not see it: a page that exists only by reference can be spelled several ways ([[Ghost Page]] on one page, [[ghost page]] on another), and TWO paths answer which spelling is shown -- DirectProjection::referenced_page_names and the Friendly SQL reader's reference_choices CTE. My set-equality proof compared the SET of raw names returned by storage, which is genuinely unchanged, so it was blind to which spelling survives the per-name fold. The old navigation statement ordered by (normalized_name, source_page_id, raw_name) and the fold takes first-wins; the Friendly CTE ordered by (p.path, raw_name, ...). Those two rules agreed only by ACCIDENT on the fixture, because the opaque source_page_id blob happened to rank the same row first as the alphabetically first path. Dropping the pages join and source_page_id -- the very thing that bought 1.276 s to 0.022 s -- broke the coincidence and friendly_main_reader_matches_the_independent_walk_for_rank_and_identity_shapes failed with the two paths naming the same page differently. Fixed by making the rule explicit and path-free on both sides: the lexicographically smallest raw spelling wins, which each path can compute from the name alone (friendly.rs reference_choices now orders by r.raw_name first; the navigation read already yields that order from the covering index). The equivalence class is provably the same on both sides: the stored normalized_name IS refs::page_key(raw_name) (direct_projection.rs:3416), and the CTE partitions by normalized_name where the fold keys by page_key(raw_name). The rule is now written at the friendly.rs CTE as a cross-path contract naming the asserting test, since nothing in docs/adr or the storage contract had ever recorded why p.path led that ordering. PROVED IN THE PROJECTION CRATE, cited here as provenance rather than as coverage because this repository's catalog gate can only resolve tests it runs: tine-storage@v0.24.0 src/sqlite_graph_projection.rs carries paged_navigation_readers_use_an_index_range, navigation_reference_names_page_without_gaps_or_repeats and fresh_build_defers_secondary_indexes_and_restores_the_exact_schema. The in-repo half of the claim is the two tests listed above; the catalog has no spelling for another repository's tests, which is a real gap and not a judgement that those three do not matter.

entries.title: A graph on an encrypted or other user-space volume opens and saves, even when the driver cannot canonicalize a path

coverage.failBefore: Structural, not same-platform. The reporter's screenshot carries the exact producer text of canonical_graph_root (src-tauri/src/state.rs): "couldn't resolve graph path: Z:\\tine\\tine-demo\\tine-demo: O volume nao contem um sistema de arquivos reconhecido ... (os error 1005)" = ERROR_UNRECOGNIZED_VOLUME from GetFinalPathNameByHandle, which is what std::fs::canonicalize calls on Windows. No Linux filesystem refuses that call, so the fallback arm is proven directly by unit test rather than by reproducing the refusal; an end-to-end Cryptomator/VeraCrypt confirmation on Windows is still outstanding.

entries.notes: Creating or opening a graph inside a Cryptomator (or VeraCrypt) vault on Windows failed with 'Couldn't create the graph. (couldn't resolve graph path ... os error 1005)', after the graph folders had already been created - so it read as a half-made graph rather than an unsupported call. Dokany/WinFsp-backed volumes are allowed not to implement GetFinalPathNameByHandle. Two sites depended on it: canonical_graph_root (the command-layer root key, which produced the reported message) and open_projection_root_nofollow (crates/tine-core/src/model/projection_fs.rs), whose failure is swallowed with .ok() - so even had the first succeeded, the graph would have opened with no projection root and every Direct save would have failed. Both now call tine_core::directory_identity::canonical_existing_path, which prefers the filesystem's canonical answer and falls back to an absolute spelling of a path that exists. Canonicalization was never the safety boundary on this path: the graph tree is opened no-follow through cap_std, which is what refuses symlinks and reparse points, and that is unchanged. One accepted consequence: on a volume that cannot canonicalize, two different spellings of one root (differing case, or a symlinked ancestor) are two different root keys rather than one.

entries.title: Export to PDF is not offered on Android or iOS, and explains itself when reached by command, instead of silently doing nothing

tests: src/pdfExportPlatform.test.ts::opens the export dialog on desktop
src/pdfExportPlatform.test.ts::explains itself instead of opening a dead dialog on android
src/pdfExportPlatform.test.ts::explains itself instead of opening a dead dialog on ios
coverage.failBefore: Both mobile cases fail on the pre-fix tree: openPdfExport set pdfExportPage to 'Alpha' on android and ios (expected null) and raised no toast, so the dialog opened and the export then did nothing. The desktop case passes before and after.

entries.notes: A mobile WebView cannot print, so print.ts's win.print() returned normally and nothing happened: no throw, hence no error toast, afterprint never fired, and the hidden frame was reclaimed by the 60 s fallback. The cause differs per platform and was read from upstream source, not inferred from behaviour. Android: AwPrintRenderFrameHelperDelegate::IsScriptedPrintEnabled returns false, so scripted printing is disabled in the WebView renderer (Chromium issue 40342444 tracks enabling it). iOS: WebKit does not guard printing - WebChromeClient::print has no PLATFORM(IOS_FAMILY) guard and UIDelegate::UIClient::printFrame has no PLATFORM(MAC) guard - but it forwards only into the private WKUIDelegate SPI _webView:printFrame:, which wry 0.55.1 does not implement (its own print() uses macOS-only printOperationWithPrintInfo:). So iOS is unimplemented rather than impossible, and a future host-side print path would lift the gate. Martin decided (2026-09-21) to gate mobile and explain, rather than implement Android printing now. The gate lives in openPdfExport, the single funnel for the page context menu, the Export current page to PDF command and its keybinding; the context-menu item is additionally hidden so no dead control is offered. Not verified on a device: no Android or iOS hardware here, so the platform claims rest on upstream source plus the jsdom gate test.

entries.title: Exporting a graph with no public pages says why nothing was exported instead of reporting a bare zero

coverage.failBefore: Not a behaviour fix: the export was already correct, and the Rust test characterises it rather than failing before. The defect was the report - Settings showed 'Exported 0 pages to <dir>' with no reason, which reads as a broken button. The message change itself is not pinned by a test; the core behaviour it describes is.

entries.notes: Reported as an Android failure, but it is neither Android-specific nor a fault. Publication is the public-page capability: only pages carrying public:: true are exported unless :publishing/all-pages-public? is set, matching Logseq (publish.rs, all_pages_public defaults to false). A graph with no public page therefore exports zero pages and writes the bare index/pages templates the reporter saw. The report was diagnosed by elimination: the UI renders 'Exported N pages' only when publishHtml RESOLVES, so a successful zero excludes both unready-projection paths, which raise errors instead - verified by running them, giving ProjectionUnavailable with no projection attached and NotReady(Busy) with a projection attached but not yet built. The Guide already documents the public:: rule (templates/research-document.md, templates/files-external-edits-backups.md); the gap was in-app, so the zero case now names the rule.

entries.title: Editing page properties does not raise a save-failure toast while they are still being typed

tests: src/store.test.ts::reconciles the store with the page header the save just wrote to disk

entries.notes: GH #546. Page-header properties authored as the flagless properties-only first bullet are folded into pre_block by the frontend projection (GH #198). That fold rewrites the file but was never reconciled into the store, so from that save on the store held the header as an ordinary root with an empty preBlock while the file held it as a preamble. The next keystroke leaving the bullet transiently not properties-only then proposed pre_block:null plus a property-bearing outline block - exactly what the GH #163 data-preservation firewall refuses. That refusal is built by projection_semantic_refusal, which carries no typed DirectSaveError, so direct_save_failure_code falls through to its Unknown default; 'unknown' is absent from the frontend's non-retryable denylist, so the save was retried at 100 ms and 300 ms and the third failure pushed the reporter's red toast, verbatim, while the block was still being edited. A successful save now marks the folded root as the page header (compare-and-swap on the exact folded text), which hands the page to the header path: it folds byte-identically and defers while invalid instead of contradicting the file. Separately, autosave no longer reports an invalid header at all - it fires shortly after a typing pause, so a half-written header is the ordinary state of an unfinished edit - and the validation message moved to where the header editor closes, which is the reporter's stated expectation. Deferring is safe only because the store now knows what the file holds: on a page whose file has no preamble the same shape still saves as outline, so an unconditional defer would have made such a page never save.

entries.title: Renaming a page costs time linear in the graph, not in referrers times folder size
entries.notes: GH #406. The reporter's timings grew faster than the graph. Cause: the portable case/NFC name check (validate_graph_text_portable_aliases_path_local) listed every entry of each ancestor directory on EVERY write, so the rename's write phase cost rewritten files x pages/ entries - measured at 0.16 ms per write on a 500-file folder, 2.2 ms at 8,000 and 4.5 ms at 16,000, about 80-85% of the write phase. The rename transaction now lists each directory once (PortableListingBatch) for its in-place referrer rewrites; a file creation (the moved page) still checks live, because a published twin cannot always be withdrawn on rollback. Fail-before: 2 vs 30 referrers listed pages/ 16 vs 72 times; after, equal. The mid-rename twin tests arm the write hook at a later mutation so the batch is provably stale; without the live creation check the destination published next to its twin and the rollback could not withdraw it (necessity run). Optimized Linux fixture, 8,000 pages: 800 referrers 2,637 ms -> 844 ms; 500/2k/8k pages 16x the pages cost 17.7x the time (was 29x). Not addressed here: every rename still reads every graph file (~5-6x the raw read floor), and the frontend reloads the whole graph afterwards (tracked with GH #535's targeted refresh). The reporter's negative follow-up on the earlier partial fix (REG-DIRECT-RENAME-LITERAL-SCANNER-406) stands; Windows latency is unmeasured.

entries.title: An empty numbered item as a page's first bullet stays a list item and the page keeps saving

tests: src/store.test.ts::stays a list item, so typing its text keeps saving
src/store.test.ts::keeps the block-scoped property list identical to the Rust promotion rule

entries.notes: GH #540, DanTremonti's report (v0.6.984, Linux): a new namespaced page, first bullet made a numbered item, then its text typed; the file stayed the 32-byte `logseq.order-list-type:: number` and every later save was refused in 0-4 ms as `reason code: unknown` until restart. Cause: the numbered-list command leaves an empty first bullet whose raw is exactly that property line, and both the frontend fold (projectPageDto) and the Rust promotion (first_root_is_promotable_page_header) took a properties-only first bullet for page-header properties (the GH #198 canonicalization), writing it as the unbulleted preamble. The typed text then moved that 'header' property back into the outline, which the GH #163 firewall refuses with an untyped error. On this branch before the fix the GH #546 reconciliation made it worse: the store adopted the fold, so the typed text was never serialized at all. OG keeps such a bullet a bullet because the property sits under an empty title line and its serializer promotes only a first block whose first line holds `:: ` (file/core.cljs transform-content); Tine's raw has no empty title line, so a block-scoped key (id, heading, collapsed, background-color, logseq.order-list-type) now disqualifies promotion on both sides, kept identical by a source guard. Reproduced byte-for-byte in core before the fix; the Rust and store numbered-item tests each fail without their half of the fix (the alias test is the GH #198 neighbour and passes either way). Not addressed: the firewall refusal is still untyped (`unknown`) and retried, so any other route into it still reads as a stuck save; EllisMorrow's original multi-day report remains unexplained.

entries.title: A save the data-preservation firewall refuses is reported once, not retried, and offers the unsaved draft

tests: src/store.test.ts::is not retried, says so once, offers the draft, and clears when the page saves
src/persistence.test.ts::does not retry failures a retry cannot change

entries.notes: Every ProjectionSemanticRefusal (merge markers, a dropped preamble, a page-header property moved into the outline, an Org file that cannot round-trip) reached the frontend as `reason code: unknown`: retried at 100/300 ms, then a transient 'after 3 tries' toast, then a page that silently never saved while each further edit repeated the cycle (GH #546 screenshot; DanTremonti's GH #540 report; the remaining gap after GH #535). The refusal is a verdict on the draft's content, so direct_save_failure_code now maps that marker type to `refused.data_preservation` (no retry) in one arm covering every producer, and the frontend shows one sticky, deduplicated message per page with a Review unsaved action (the close-path recovery panel: Copy draft, Open page), dismissed when the page saves or leaves the working set. Fail-before: the core tests return `unknown`; the store test sees 6 save attempts instead of 4 without the frontend policy change. The firewall itself is unchanged.

entries.title: A save conflict whose one-shot review authority was revoked early can still be captured, reviewed after a restart, and resolved
entries.notes: User outcome: after a save conflict, the banner 'Your draft and the current file both changed' stayed up but its comparison failed with 'live conflict authority is missing or already consumed' -- and after a restart it failed on every attempt, with no way to clear it. Mechanism (verified in core): a refused save mints a process-local one-shot token; any watcher reconcile of that path (sync_file_checked, including the echo of the write that caused the conflict) and, on Windows, any uncertain delete/rename anywhere in the graph (revoke_all_conflict_authority) revokes it. Landing between the refusal and capture_live_save_conflict, the capture failed, the capsule was stored without disk_rev, and the review routed to the dead token forever. Fix: the token is a preference, never a precondition -- a capture whose token is gone is taken from the disk as it is now (with the editor's loaded base when this process still has it), and a capsule without disk_rev whose token is gone (restart, or a Managed-era epoch -1) is reviewed durably. Apply still rechecks the displayed disk revision under the page lock, so nothing is authorized that the durable path did not already allow; the revocation rules are unchanged. Fail-before: with both fallbacks disabled, the capture test panics at the capture and the restore test at the review. Scope note: the reporter's own v0.6.982 failure is more likely the file-absent-under-a-captured-draft case fixed by a1f0c512 (v0.6.983); this row covers the remaining mechanism, found while investigating #490. Not run natively on Windows.

entries.title: A page that is also hard-linked elsewhere (git-annex, deduplication) can be renamed, restored after a crash, and edited externally without discarding the warm index

coverage.failBefore: On the pre-fix tree: a_hard_linked_page_can_be_renamed failed 'annex: graph text files alias one physical resource: pages/Old.md has link count 2'; an_external_edit_to_a_hard_linked_page_keeps_the_identity_index_warm reported invalidated: true, exact_updates: 0; the recovery test's predecessor pinned that checked open REFUSED the graph.

entries.notes: After the save fix, three paths still refused on a raw link count. (1) The rename transaction's move source and editor recovery: a move keeps the inode, so no name can diverge, and the MS-REF-GRAPH-TEXT-ALIAS divergence comes only from temp+rename publication, so the check defended nothing; the referrer rewrites are ordinary publications, already allowed. (2) The checked-open recovery sweep refused the WHOLE graph over a recovery artifact with a second link, which git-annex's assistant produces under .git/annex/watchtmp. (3) The exact watcher delta required link count 1 while a complete build admits any, so every external edit of an annexed graph discarded the warm identity index and the next create or rename paid a whole-graph rebuild. All three now accept a link outside graph-text scope. Two GRAPH pages on one inode stay refused where the sibling can be named (Martin, 2026-09-20): the rename inventory refuses with both paths and changes nothing (asserted in the rename test), and an exact delta with resources.len() != 1 falls back to a rebuild. Windows/Google Drive (GH #571) is covered structurally: the Windows link count comes from GetFileInformationByHandle and no path now refuses on it; not run on Windows.

entries.title: Opening a page while the index is being checked at launch does not force a whole-graph parse
entries.notes: GH #543 warm-reopen follow-up. The launch-time warm validation reads every page to confirm the stored index is current (5.6 s for 10,000 pages on the Windows verify runner). Opening today's journal meanwhile publishes the page even when its bytes are unchanged; that moved the cache generation, the warm abandoned on drift, and every warm reopen fell back to a whole-graph parse (16 s to a working search, run 35643784742). A generation move made only of one-page publications whose session revisions equal what the warm read no longer discards it: removals and whole-cache invalidations move a separate structural counter and still count as drift. gh543_a_page_opened_during_the_warm_read_keeps_the_warm fails on the old any-move rule (unchanged case parses the whole graph) and checks that an edit or a new page written during the warm is indexed. Windows re-measure pending.

entries.title: Whole-graph views opened during the launch-time index check wait for it instead of parsing every page
entries.notes: GH #543 warm-reopen follow-up (Windows verify run 35648984084: 10k warm reopen 24.9 s vs 16.0 s before). During the warm validation read the projection queue is idle and the worker not busy, so the 250 ms readiness wait returned false at once and the launch-time page list and alias reads parsed the whole graph; that installed a full snapshot which outranked the warm and was indexed after it. Page inventory, aliases, property owner rows and block ref counts now wait while the projection reports the warm in flight and no parsed cache exists. Two launch gaps fed the same parse: the app delays its warm thread 250 ms so the first paint goes first, and that paint's page list found no warm announced; and opening today's journal moved the generation under a waiting read, which then gave up. The warm is now announced when it is scheduled (held for the life of its thread, so a read cannot wait on a warm nobody runs) and a waiting read follows generation moves. Local release app on a 10k-page graph: ready at 1.4 s with no full snapshot, previously 2.7 s with one. Both tests fail on the corresponding old behaviour and check the answers with zero parses. Evidence: tine-agents/evidence/gh550-batch/gh543-derived-wait/.

entries.title: Opening an unchanged page during a first open's page-reading pass does not discard the pass
entries.notes: GH #543 indexing audit IT-04. Opening a page publishes it and moves the cache generation even when its bytes are unchanged (the publication re-lowers the page with this session's block ids, which the stored index may not carry). The cold page-reading pass installed only at its exact starting generation, so opening today's journal while it ran discarded the pass and the next reader parsed the whole graph again. Installation now uses the rule the warm check already uses: no structural move, and every page published this session has the revision and config the pass read. An edit after the pass read the page still discards it. The first test fails when installation requires the exact generation. Evidence: tine-agents/evidence/gh550-batch/gh543-derived-wait/cold-install-fail-before.log.

entries.title: Page icons, block references, referrers, templates, calendar days and property facets answer from the index on reopen without parsing the graph
entries.notes: GH #543 indexing audit IT-01. Rendering a page link (icon), a block reference or embed (resolve/preview), a block's referrers, the template picker, the calendar and property facets each called the whole-graph parser, even with a current index, so a warm reopen that needed zero parses parsed every page and enqueued a full snapshot. They now answer from SQL (candidate blocks only, reconstructed per call, nothing retained), wait for the warm check instead of parsing before ready, and follow a generation move (a page opened during the read) by re-reading the index: Graph::indexed_read is the one front door, pinned by a source-count guard. Runtime block ids the index does not hold are located through session_page_ids and hydrate one page; load_by_path now records them. Duplicate claimants resolve in path order (the parser used read_dir order). Each surface's answer equals the parser oracle on a fixture with aliases, upper-case ref spelling, nested and child-only templates, empty/property-only/renamed journals. Fail-before: every surface parsed 8-9 pages; with a page opened mid-read, all six parsed the whole graph. Evidence: tine-agents/evidence/gh550-batch/bl1/.

entries.title: A launch-time index check is not discarded because pages opened at launch are still queued for indexing
entries.notes: GH #543 indexing audit IT-03 (queued-update half). Opening a page at launch queues an index update. enqueue_warm refused a warm whenever any update was queued, and the warm itself waited at most 2 s for the queue to drain; on the realistic 10k graph the worker had not taken three launch updates when the warm read finished at 1.4 s, so the warm was refused and the whole graph was parsed (full snapshot at +4.7 s). The worker already validates a warm and applies updates after it in one turn, so the queue now takes the warm beside updates at or below its generation and the drain wait is gone. If validation finds the stored index stale, the updates taken with the warm are requeued instead of dropped, so readiness is never published without them. The test holds the worker so an update stays queued at hand-over; it parsed 9 pages before the fix. A real edit during the warm still takes the parser path (the rest of IT-03). Evidence: tine-agents/evidence/gh550-batch/it03-warm-beside-deltas-fail-before.log.

entries.title: Editing or creating a page during the launch-time index check does not send the graph to a whole-graph parse
entries.notes: GH #543 indexing audit IT-03 (real-edit half). A page edited or created after the warm read it published an update, but the warm treated any publication at other bytes as drift, abandoned its read and the whole graph was parsed (9 parses on a 9-page fixture). The warm now keeps its read across any non-structural move; pages this session published at bytes other than it read are passed as `published`, validation leaves their stored rows alone, and their queued updates are applied after it. A new page's update taken by the worker before the warm arrived could not be placed without an inventory and latched a fresh build (10 parses); it is now parked until the warm or full snapshot seeds the page order. Neighbour fixed in the same change: a page the walk could not read was appended to the page order, shifting every later page onto a position another stored page held, so the next ordinary edit failed the worker (UNIQUE pages.position) and rebuilt the index; the warm now seeds the walk's own order. Removals and invalidations still discard the read. Evidence: tine-agents/evidence/gh550-batch/it03-real-edit-fail-before*.

entries.title: Reopening a graph after a few pages changed elsewhere re-indexes only those pages
entries.notes: GH #543 indexing audit IT-03 (between-sessions half; Martin chose bounded repair 2026-09-22). One page edited, added or deleted between sessions made warm validation return fresh-build-required, and the whole graph was parsed and relowered (17 whole-graph parses on the fixture; +20.3 s to ready on the realistic 10k graph). Validation now names the changed pages when the walk is complete and at most a quarter changed; exactly those are parsed and applied in one transaction with page order reconciled, then validated again before readiness. Neighbours fixed in the same change: a launch read of a new page queued positions from the walk order before the repair, collided on pages.position and failed the worker into a fresh build; and an update for bytes the repair already wrote was lowered twice. Evidence: tine-agents/evidence/gh550-batch/it03-between-sessions-fail-before.log.

entries.title: Opening a named page does not wait for launch-time indexing
entries.notes: GH #543 indexing audit IT-05. load_named resolved every named page through find_entry, which needs the graph-wide page list, so a restored tab, home page, favourite or link waited for the launch warm (3.9 s on the realistic 10k graph during a cold build). A page is now opened from the file named for it when exactly one such file exists and its effective name matches; otherwise the list is used as before. find_entry now prefers the file named for a page over one claiming its name via title::, so both paths resolve the same file; both halves proven necessary. Evidence: tine-agents/evidence/gh550-batch/it05-named-open-fail-before.log, it05-named-open-10k.md.

entries.title: Creating a page after reopening or during launch indexing does not parse the whole graph
entries.notes: GH #543 indexing audit IT-02. Name-only creation needs evidence that no other document owns the effective name. With no parsed cache (every clean reopen), direct_creation_proof ran repair_page_cache_once: a whole-graph parse and cache install on the save path, ahead of the launch warm when one ran (6 parses on the fixture; 10,000 parses and 416 ms on the realistic 10k graph). Evidence now comes from the ready index's effective page inventory, waiting for an in-flight launch check like other derived reads, and falls back to the parsed evidence only when no ready index answers or a parse failure is published. A name owned via title:: is still refused. Evidence: tine-agents/evidence/gh550-batch/it02-creation-fail-before.log, it02-creation-10k.md.
